title: Trump admin cannot refuse detained illegal immigrants a chance for release on bond, appeals court rules
summary: A federal appeals court ruled against the Trump administration's expanded mandatory detention policy adopted as part of its mass deportation plan.
story: A federal judge in Boston ruled against the Trump administration's $100,000 fee for H-1B visas, deeming it an unauthorized tax. The fee, which was significantly increased from a typical $2,000-$5,000, aimed to prioritize US citizens in the workforce. The administration is appealing the decision.
A federal appeals court on Thursday ruled that the Trump administration cannot deny migrants detained inside the U.S. a chance for release on bond as part of its expanded mandatory detention policy.
In a 2-1 decision, the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals in San Francisco ruled against the administration.
Four other appeals courts have also rejected the policy, although the Fifth Circuit in New Orleans and Eighth Circuit in St. Louis have ruled in favor of the federal government.
The deepening circuit split raises the chance that the U.S. Supreme Court will eventually take up the case. The administration asked the high court last month to consider the case.
APPEALS COURT BLOCKS TRUMP ADMIN FROM HOLDING MIGRANTS WITHOUT BOND FOR 90 DAYS
A federal appeals court ruled that the Trump administration cannot deny migrants detained inside the U.S. a chance for release on bond. (Jim WATSON / AFP via Getty Images)
The Department of Homeland Security said it "strongly disagrees with the Ninth Circuit panel and is confident in its legal position regarding mandatory detention."
"President Donald Trump and Secretary Mullin are now enforcing the law as it was actually written to keep America safe," the department said in a statement.

Under previous administrations, most illegal immigrants with no criminal record who were arrested inside the U.S. were allowed to seek a bond hearing while their immigration cases were pending, and mandatory detention was typically reserved for those detained at the border.

But last year, the government issued guidance expanding mandatory detention to include illegal immigrants inside the U.S. The move was part of the president's mass deportation plan, leading to several lawsuits by immigrants pursuing a release from custody.
The Department of Homeland Security said it "strongly disagrees with the Ninth Circuit panel and is confident in its legal position regarding mandatory detention." (Kevin Carter/Getty Images)
Some federal judges who ordered bond hearings criticized the administration for repeatedly violating their orders.
The administration has said that Congress changed immigration law in 1996 to allow mandatory detention past the border and that previous administrations failed to enforce that measure.
But Ninth Circuit Judge Daniel Bress, who was appointed by President Donald Trump, rejected that argument.

"Although no reading of the complicated and interrelated textual provisions at issue here is without some shortcomings, the historical understanding of the statute is the better one," said Bress, writing for the majority.
DEMOCRAT COMPARES ICE TO 'DOMESTIC TERRORISTS' AS 111 HOUSE DEMS DEMAND TEXAS DETENTION CENTER CLOSE
Some federal judges who ordered bond hearings criticized the administration for repeatedly violating their orders. (Spencer Platt/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Bress was joined by Judge M. Margaret McKeown, who was appointed by former President Bill Clinton.
Judge Carlos Bea, who was appointed by President George W. Bush, dissented, arguing that the amendment Congress passed 30 years ago supports the administration's position.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

title: GOP gubernatorial candidate fighting to flip blue state unveils healthcare plan to lower costs, expand access
summary: Massachusetts GOP hopeful Mike Minogue outlines a healthcare overhaul centered on innovation, outpatient care, mental health and cutting waste.
story: Gubernatorial candidate Mike Minogue explains how he would expand access, lower costs, tackle the mental health crisis and root out waste in the state's healthcare system.
EXCLUSIVE: While Massachusetts boasts some of the premier hospitals in the world, it also suffers from some of the highest healthcare costs in America.
GOP gubernatorial candidate Mike Minogue believes that is no coincidence.

In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, the former longtime medical devices CEO says the commonwealth can boost access, cut costs and reduce regulation through innovation as opposed to government mandates.
MIKE MINOGUE HEADS TO MASS GOP CONVENTION READY TO TAKE ON MAURA HEALEY: 'SHE'S BANKRUPTING OUR STATE'
Combat veteran-turned-CEO Mike Minogue launched a Republican campaign for governor in Massachusetts Wednesday. (Mike Minogue campaign)

"I think the most important thing that can help health care is to have a 'patients first mindset.' When I was the CEO of Abiomed, everyone rallied around the patients-first culture, commitment and every action.

"Every decision that we took really was focused on, ‘Does this improve the patient outcome? Does this help the physicians and the nurses make it easier to use? Does it help us save money for the system?’"
He cited the weighty regulatory burden imposed on nurses and doctors as part of the problem.

"We [must] have a focus that we're really going through areas that allow for patients to get access to their physicians, their nurses, and also utilize innovation, things that are breakthrough and things that can minimize the burden on the physicians and the nurses with regulations and documentation.

"I'm optimistic because I've seen it firsthand. I've worked with healthcare systems all over the world. I specifically know how hard physicians and nurses work, and they're the heart of that system. So, what we're going to focus on is a patients-first health care plan that brings access to quality, affordable care."

Healthcare is a top concern for Bay State voters, and Minogue hopes to use the issue to his advantage in a tough battle to challenge incumbent Democrat Gov. Maura Healey.He notes that the often stark disparity between healthcare access and quality between the metro Boston area and the rest of the state is a perpetual problem that needs a remedy.

"Right now, if you look at what's happening around Massachusetts, we're losing innovation and treatment in areas that do not now have opportunity for high-risk procedures, whether it's maternity, cardiac or stroke.

"We have areas now in communities that might have a 50-plus minute drive to get to the nearest area. An example is Norwood. The hospital closed. So, if you have a cardiac event in Norwood, you're looking at a 55-minute-plus drive at best to get to Boston."
Massachusetts Gov. Maura Healey also hosted a news conference Thursday, pushing back on the Supreme Court's decision. (David L. Ryan/The Boston Globe via Getty Images)
Minogue promises that, during his tenure, he will work to improve coverage and care statewide.
"This is the role of the governor — to provide hub-and-spoke innovation in healthcare for the whole commonwealth, not just Boston."
COMBAT VETERAN TURNED CEO HAS A NEW MISSION: FLIP GOVERNOR'S OFFICE IN BLUE STATE
Yet, Minogue argues, the current system poses not merely a geographic problem, but a fiscal one.

"Our regulations strangle the rest of the commonwealth and almost mandate that all procedures are being done in Boston in the highest-cost environment. If you go to outpatient centers and surgery centers, you reduce the cost of procedures, you lower the overhead and it's a much easier process than driving all the way into Boston. We have incredible hospitals here, but we also have some of the lowest numbers of outpatient clinics and surgery centers as a state. We need to improve that."Given his business background, Minogue is intimately familiar with the economics of providing healthcare coverage for thousands of families.
"As a CEO, I bought health insurance for 19 years for my employees. I never saw an increase that wasn't double-digit every year. … We need to lower the costs.
"We also have to minimize mandating every single treatment and procedure onto every healthcare plan. We need to allow people to have the ability to select what care they want."
FOX NEWS POLL: GOP DIVISIONS SHAPE TEXAS SENATE RACE
Minogue believes patients should have more flexibility in choosing their coverage while ensuring families are protected from financially devastating medical emergencies.

"We do need to cap the catastrophic. … At Abiomed, what we did every year is we paid the extra amount so that we would always cap what it would cost the patient. We combined that with a health savings account, which is a great way for people to take more control over their own healthcare plan. Everything that you do in a patient's first mindset solves a lot of problems."With a mental health crisis surging across the state, Minogue has a solution for matching patients and therapists.

"We do have an extensive amount of counselors, but most of them are on private pay. … We don't allow general practitioners or counselors to get paid outside of private pay, so that's why most of these patients are going to the emergency rooms.
"It would be simple and more efficient if we also allowed the subsidized government pay to allow those patients to see the same people in the clinics that private-pay people have access to."
Republican Mike Minogue, with his wife Renee and their five children, is running for the Republican gubernatorial nomination in Massachusetts  (Mike Minogue campaign)
Minogue's plan has specific provisions for addressing an area where the mental health crisis has been particularly acute.
"One of the areas that I'm most focused on for mental health or PTSD is our correctional facility officers in Massachusetts have some of the highest suicide rates in America.
"We know veterans with PTSD also have high suicide rates. These people are all ending up in emergency rooms, and that's not a very good solution."
Hands-on experience with frontline healthcare workers is what Minogue believes gives his plan the credibility to set the Bay State on the right track again.
"I've been very fortunate because I have a network of physicians and nurses and counselors that have been working with me for months.
"We've collaborated so that we can come up with this patients-first plan.

"If you put the patient at the center of that, the treatment plans can be very specialized for better outcomes at lower cost."Finally, Minogue has a specific plan to root out waste and fraud, a particularly timely topic following investigations across the nation that have unveiled a costly web of corruption in social services at the taxpayer's expense.

"The most important thing is to recognize that better outcomes and a patients-first mindset actually can reduce costs. … But we have an additional area of cost savings. It's called inefficiency, waste and fraud.
CLICK HERE TO GET THE FOX NEWS APP
"We'll identify inefficiency, excess and fraud, and I believe we're going to find hundreds of millions of dollars in savings at a minimum.
"I'd like to use some of that money as an incentive on outcomes and make sure physicians and nurses can share in the success of improving outcomes. Great quality will lower our costs."

Minogue won the Massachusetts GOP endorsement at the party's state convention in Worcester and is widely expected to win the Republican primary Sept. 1 to face off against incumbent Gov. Maura Healey.

title: WATCH: GOP holdout rejects Trump threat as AG nominee standoff explodes
summary: Thom Tillis dismissed Trump's threat to withdraw Todd Blanche's nomination for attorney general, saying the White House must honor a prior commitment.
story: Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., responds to President Trump's threat to pull Todd Blanche's nomination, saying negotiations continue and blaming the White House for the stalled confirmation process. (Credit: Nicholas Ballasy for Fox News Digital)

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., brushed aside President Donald Trump's threat to withdraw acting Attorney General Todd Blanche's nomination Thursday, arguing the White House must instead honor what he says was an earlier commitment to win his vote.
"That's his prerogative," Tillis said of Trump’s threat to withdraw Blanche’s nomination.

Tillis’ comments come after Trump called out both Tillis and Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, on Truth Social Thursday morning for blocking the president’s efforts to make Blanche the nation’s top prosecutor.
Trump then threatened to pull Blanche’s nomination until the two Republican senators leave office next year. Tillis is retiring, and Cornyn lost his primary in his run for re-election.
TRUMP THREATENS TO YANK HIS OWN AG NOMINEE AS GOP REVOLT GROWS

Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., is brushing off President Donald Trump's threat to pull Todd Blanche's nomination, insisting negotiations remain ongoing. (Nathan Posner/Anadolu via Getty Images; Ken Cedeno/AFP via Getty Images)
Tillis argued Trump cannot resolve this nomination standoff "unless we fulfill what we thought was the commitment from the administration."

The North Carolina senator has withheld his support for Blanche unless the administration agrees to permanently eliminate the nearly $2 billion anti-weaponization fund and rewrite Trump's audit immunity language in a settlement agreement. Negotiations over those demands remain ongoing.
"The best thing is, take the win, get Blanche confirmed and get this agreement out of the way," Tillis told Fox News Digital.
When asked what it would take to get Tillis to vote to confirm Blanche, he said, "exactly what Blanche committed to."
TRUMP ADMIN PUSHES BACK ON 'SLUSH FUND' ATTACKS AGAINST ANTI-WEAPONIZATION FUND AND LAYS OUT WHO QUALIFIES
Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche appears at a confirmation hearing before the Senate Judiciary Committee on Capitol Hill in Washington, D.C., July 15, 2026. (Eric Lee/Getty Images)
Tillis stressed that Blanche is not to blame for the impasse, saying he believes he "was honest" during his confirmation process and that he blames someone on Trump’s team.
"This is not Blanche's problem. It's clear to me that Blanche was honest when he answered without hesitation, working with us to end this," Tillis said.
"I believe that one of the president's advisors who were part of this agreement is the problem. And they need to own it."

Tillis also pointed out that there is no certainty that the Senate would be any more accepting of Blanche next year, particularly as Republicans have more seats in danger than Democrats in the Senate.
"The best-case scenario is you come back with the same number of people next year, and our members are not going to be any more supportive of this than they are today."
TRUMP-TILLIS TIFF DEEPENS AS PRESIDENT SAYS HE ‘QUIT,’ CONCEDES FED FIGHT COULD DOOM NEW CHAIR CONFIRMATION
Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., makes his way to a vote in the U.S. Capitol on Thursday, April 30, 2026. (Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc)

Trump could still keep Blanche as acting attorney general for months even if he withdraws the nomination. The Federal Vacancies Reform Act allows acting officials to serve for 210 days, and withdrawing a pending nomination resets that clock. If Trump were to pull Blanche's nomination Thursday, Blanche could remain in the role until late February.
Despite Trump's public threat, Tillis said negotiations with the administration remain ongoing and said he is "not a no" on Blanche.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"In this place, nothing's ever as good or as bad as it seems, so we're continuing to negotiate," Tillis said.
Fox News Digital’s Alex Miller and Adam Pack contributed to this report.
Hannah is a Production Assistant for the Politics team at Fox News Digital.

title: Mamdani's 'this is only the beginning' announcement cracking down on food delivery tips sparks outrage
summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani faced viral backlash Thursday over a post claiming responsibility for increasing food delivery service tips.
story: Fox News correspondent Alexis McAdams discusses the rise of Zohran Mamdani and his allies with New Yorkers.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani is facing fresh criticism after taking credit for a reported $104 million increase in delivery worker tips that critics say was made possible by legislation enacted before he took office and will likely only exacerbate cost of living issues in the city.

The criticism comes after Mamdani declared at a press conference Wednesday and in a social media post, "We've put $104 million back in delivery workers' pockets," citing changes to Uber Eats' and DoorDash's apps that made tipping more prominent.
"This is only the beginning," Mamdani wrote.

Those changes stem from a city law approved by the New York City Council before Mamdani became mayor. Former Mayor Eric Adams neither signed nor vetoed the measure, allowing it to become law after 30 days. The rules took effect in January under the Mamdani administration, which implemented and enforced the requirements.
MAMDANI'S 'RATION SHOP' GROCERY PLAN FACES BLISTERING ECONOMIC CRITIQUE AS OPPONENTS BLAST SOCIALIST POLICY
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani speaks to reporters during a news conference in New York on Feb. 17, 2026.  (AP Photo/Seth Wenig)

Before the law took effect, the New York City Department of Consumer and Worker Protection found that Uber Eats and DoorDash had hidden tip buttons and set default tips below 10%, contributing to a 79% decline in tips for delivery workers. The law required the companies to make tipping more prominent, and city officials say the resulting changes have since generated an estimated $104 million in additional tips.

Mamdani's office rejected the criticism that the mayor was taking credit for someone else's work, arguing that while the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection pushed for the reforms before he took office, the rules were implemented under his administration beginning Jan. 26.

"A law is only as good as its implementation," a spokesperson for Mamdani told Fox News Digital. "We have been intentional about enforcing the laws on the books so that we are putting money back into the pockets of working New Yorkers."

Conservatives and political commentators on social media quickly blasted Mamdani for the already high costs of goods and services in New York City, and some accused the mayor of taking credit for legislation that was born before his term.

"This guy is a fantastic lying politician," actor Michael Rapaport posted on X. "He had literally nothing to do with this. City Council passed the bill last August and 419 Eric Adams never signed it. 30 days the bill became law. It went into effect when Mamdani was in office. He just taking the credit."
MAMDANI'S RENT FREEZE, TAX HIKES A 'ONE-TWO WEALTH DESTRUCTION PUNCH,' ECONOMISTS WARN
In this photo illustration, a person demonstrates making a delivery with DoorDash as a Dasher in April 2024 in San Francisco. (Emily Dulla/Getty Images for DoorDash)

title: Hamas agrees to complete disarmament under 'historic' Gaza agreement: Trump
summary: President Donald Trump announced what he called a historic agreement to completely disarm Hamas and other armed groups in Gaza as part of a broader peace initiative.
story: Fox News Flash top headlines are here. Check out what's clicking on FoxNews.com.
President Donald Trump on Thursday announced a historic agreement for the complete disarmament of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza.
The diplomatic breakthrough, brokered by his Board of Peace alongside mediators Egypt, Qatar and Turkey, will pave the way for a new Palestinian government in Gaza, Trump said.

"Today, the Board of Peace reached a HISTORIC agreement for the COMPLETE DISARMAMENT of Hamas and all other armed groups in Gaza. This is a monumental step toward lasting PEACE and SECURITY," Trump said in a Truth Social post.
HAMAS SAYS IT WILL DISSOLVE GAZA GOVERNMENT, BUT ISRAEL WARNS GROUP STILL SEEKS HEZBOLLAH-STYLE CONTROL
Trump unveiled a Gaza peace agreement calling for the complete disarmament of Hamas and other armed groups. (Joe Raedle/Getty Images)
The agreement represents a "major milestone" in implementing Trump’s 20-Point Plan, a framework introduced last year aimed at ending the war and rebuilding Gaza.
The president said the multiphased disarmament agreement marks a "critical step" toward Gaza being governed by a new Palestinian government with the support of the Board of Peace.
He added the city will no longer be used as "a base for terror attacks."
A new police force will also be established in Gaza with the support of the International Stabilization Force, keeping the region "safe for its residents and its neighbors."
ISRAEL'S MILITARY ELIMINATES HAMAS TERRORIST WHO HELPED ABDUCT AMERICAN-ISRAELI HOSTAGE, 3 OTHERS
Trump said Thursday's deal marks a major step toward lasting peace, with Gaza no longer serving as a base for terror attacks. (AP/Alex Brandon/Majdi Fathi/NurPhoto via Getty Images)
Israeli forces will withdraw from the region as the disarmament process moves forward through the structured phases.
Trump praised the progress his administration has made since Hamas-led militants carried out a deadly assault on southern Israel from the Gaza Strip Oct. 7, 2023.

"One year ago there was a violent raging war, humanitarian crisis and hostages kept in brutal captivity. We have made historic progress and there is still much work to do," Trump said. "The threat that emerged from Gaza on October 7 will NOT be allowed to rebuild!
"Under this agreement, Gaza will finally be in the hands of a new Palestinian government that serves its PEOPLE."
Members of Hamas during a parade of the terror group in Gaza Jan. 25, 2025. (TPS-IL)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Trump further thanked all the parties involved in the historic agreement.
"I want to thank the mediators — Egypt, Qatar, and Türkiye — for their important efforts, and especially my outstanding team, whose tireless work made this historic breakthrough possible."
Hours later, the Board of Peace released a statement saying the agreement holds significant "promise" for a better future across Gaza and Israel.

"For the first time, Hamas officially has committed to an actionable plan for relinquishing all its weapons, which will be followed by Israeli withdrawal from Gaza. It holds the promise of delivering significant benefits to the people of Gaza, who have waited for too long for a better future, and security to the people of Israel," the Board of Peace said in a post on X.

The Board of Peace said the next phase will focus on implementation, with Gaza beginning a phased transition toward "full authority," while accelerating efforts to establish the rule of law, improve security and advance humanitarian conditions.

"The agreement concludes months of intensive, good faith negotiations to advance President Donald J. Trump's vision for establishing new governance, security, humanitarian relief, reconstruction, and economic recovery in Gaza as set out in the Comprehensive Peace Plan and U.N. Security Council Resolution 2803."
Bonny Chu is a Breaking and Trending News Writer for Fox News Digital

title: Schiff-backed candidate abruptly ends gubernatorial campaign amid rumblings of a damaging report
summary: Mandela Barnes suspended his Wisconsin gubernatorial campaign amid a crowded Democratic primary, leaving Francesca Hong and David Crowley as major contenders.
story: Wisconsin Democratic gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong was asked about appearing on far-left Twitch streamer Hasan Piker's livestream on MS NOW Wednesday.
Mandela Barnes, who served as lieutenant governor of Wisconsin from 2019 to 2023, suspended his gubernatorial campaign Thursday, citing a lack of support to capture the Democratic Party nomination.
"It’s become very clear who our nominee is going to be," Barnes said in a video statement.
"While I may be suspending my campaign, I’ll never give up my fight for Wisconsin."
WISCONSIN DEM SOCIALIST GUBERNATORIAL HOPEFUL DODGES WHETHER SHE STILL WANTS TO ‘ABOLISH POLICE’
Mandela Barnes leaves a canvas launch event Nov. 7, 2022, in Glendale, Wis. (Scott Olson/Getty Images)

Barnes, who was endorsed by Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., as the "kind of bold leader we need to take on the Trump administration," did not name the candidate he believes will capture the party’s nomination later this month.

His departure from the race comes as a surprise amid a crowded Democratic field to fill the empty seat of outgoing Democratic Gov. Tony Evers. Barnes was considered a frontrunner in the race because of his proximity to Evers and his name recognition.

It also coincides with rumblings that Barnes may have abused his position in the past to make sexual advances toward women in the workplace, an allegation currently under investigation by The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel, which published its report shortly after Barnes' video post.

Barnes' campaign did not immediately respond to a request for comment on whether his decision to suspend the campaign was in any way connected to the reporting. However, a Barnes spokesperson told Politico "there are no allegations of misconduct or wrongdoing against Mandela."
With Barnes’ departure, the remaining major candidates include Wisconsin state Rep. Francesca Hong, a democratic socialist, and Milwaukee County Executive David Crowley.
TOP DEM HOPEFUL FLIPS SCRIPT AFTER YEARS IN SOCIALIST ORBIT WITH PUZZLING CLAIM
Congressman Adam Schiff speaks at the Just Majority Burbank Press Conference on May 26, 2023, in Los Angeles.  (Jerod Harris/Getty Images for Demand Justice)

Hong has received backing from a number of nationally recognized progressives, including Rep. Ilhan Omar, D-Minn., and Rep. Ro Khanna, D-Calif. She had raised nearly $709,000 as of late June, according to state records.
By comparison, Crowley has secured $250,000 and enjoys the support of a number of local organizations and figures.
Evers, pointedly, endorsed Crowley over Barnes, citing Crowley’s experience.
In his departure video, Barnes urged Democrats to unite against Republicans in the November general election.

"Now, I said from the very beginning when I launched this campaign that the No. 1 goal was taking on and defeating Tom Tiffany to deliver big wins for Democrats up and down the ticket," Barnes said, referring to the presumptive Republican nominee.

"Now it’s our time to come together and focus our efforts on that one goal. We have to do everything to beat Tom Tiffany. This is life or death for Wisconsinites who are losing their healthcare under a Trump administration."
SCOTT WALKER: DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS ARE COMING FOR MY STATE. THIS IS HOW WE BEAT THEM
Rep. Tom Tiffany, R-Wis., speaks during a television interview outside of the Capitol after being sworn in as a member of Congress May 19, 2020. (Bill Clark/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Barnes built his campaign on a platform of increasing taxes on the country’s top earners, freezing energy costs, providing universal childcare and lowering the cost of housing.
The gubernatorial primary will take place Aug. 11.
Leo Briceno is a politics reporter for the congressional team at Fox News Digital. He was previously a reporter with World Magazine.

title: Fox News Poll: GOP divisions shape Texas Senate race
summary: Ken Paxton trails James Talarico by three points in the Texas Senate race as character concerns and a GOP unity gap reshape the 2026 midterm battle.
story: Harris Faulkner hosts a 'Voters' Voices' panel, exploring voter motivation, top midterm issues like the economy and the rise of socialism.

President Donald Trump won the Lone Star state by nearly 14 percentage points in 2024, but a new Fox News Poll of Texas registered voters suggests this year's Senate race is far less settled. Republican Senate candidate Ken Paxton has yet to fully unify the GOP despite the president’s endorsement in the GOP primary against incumbent Sen. John Cornyn.

In addition, more voters are concerned Paxton lacks the character to serve than worry Democratic challenger James Talarico is too extreme, and more Democrats than Republicans are extremely motivated to vote (by 7 points) and extremely interested in the midterms (by 6).
Those dynamics give Talarico a 3-point edge over Paxton (51% vs. 48%) in the Senate contest (within the survey’s margin of sampling error).
Talarico's advantage in the race grows to 6 points among both extremely motivated and extremely interested voters (53% vs. 47% in each group).
FOX NEWS POLL: DEMOCRATIC ENTHUSIASM SHAPES NORTH CAROLINA SENATE RACE
Most independents (68%) and virtually all Democrats support Talarico (98%), while fewer Republicans are unified behind Paxton (89%).
In part, that’s because one quarter of non-MAGA Republicans back Talarico (24%).
Paxton is the choice among White evangelical Christians, White men without a college degree, rural voters, regular worship attenders, men and voters ages 65 and older.
Some of Talarico’s best groups are Black voters, moderates, voters under age 30, Hispanic voters, women and voters with a college degree.
"Although Paxton dominated Cornyn in the GOP primary, that bruising contest left scars," said Republican pollster Daron Shaw, who conducts Fox News polls with Democrat Chris Anderson.
"He has considerable work to do with non-MAGA Republicans and independents, and that undoubtedly requires aggressively tying Talarico to the Democratic Party’s far left."
By a 12-point margin, more voters are concerned Paxton lacks the character to serve as a senator than believe Talarico is too extreme (59% vs. 47%).
Twice as many Republicans are concerned about Paxton's character as Democrats are that Talarico is too extreme (36% vs. 17%).
FOX NEWS POLL: COOL YOUR SERVERS! VOTERS REJECT DATA CENTERS
Still, about 8 in 10 Paxton and Talarico supporters say their backing is more about where the candidates stand on the issues than who they are as people.

Trump received a 55% favorable vs. 44% unfavorable rating in the 2024 Texas Fox News Voter Analysis (FNVA) election survey. Today, those numbers have flipped: 45% favorable vs. 54% unfavorable, for a minus-9 net negative rating.
Paxton garners a minus-6 net personal rating, 45% favorable vs. 51% unfavorable, while Talarico is in positive territory by 6 points, 49% vs. 43%.
Talarico is more popular than the Democratic Party while the GOP edges out Paxton.
While both parties are viewed negatively, the GOP is underwater by only 2 points (48% favorable vs. 50% unfavorable), compared with the Democratic Party at minus-9 (45% vs. 54%).

Despite Texas being a border state, nearly 4 in 10 say inflation will be the most important issue to their Senate vote, while 2 in 10 say immigration and 1 in 10 say healthcare, political divisions and unemployment.
By more than a 2-to-1 margin, Texas voters say they are falling behind financially rather than getting ahead (35% vs. 16%). Half are holding steady.
In the race for governor, incumbent Republican Gov. Greg Abbott is favored by 1 point over Democrat Gina Hinojosa.
Part of Abbott's edge comes from a touch more crossover support: 12% of Talarico supporters back Abbott, while 9% of Paxton supporters back Hinojosa.
Hinojosa has the advantage among extremely motivated (+6) and extremely interested voters (+5).

Abbott has a net positive personal rating by a single point (50% favorable vs. 49% unfavorable). Hinojosa is in positive territory by 11 points (45% vs. 34%), although nearly 1 in 5 are unable to rate her.
Texas last elected a Democratic governor in 1990 (Ann Richards), a Democratic Senator in 1988 (Lloyd Bentsen), and a Democratic presidential candidate in 1976 (Jimmy Carter).
A closer look at the Hispanic electorate

Hispanic voters say their Senate pick will be driven by inflation, as roughly 4 in 10 say it will be the most important issue to their vote and another 4 in 10 say they’re falling behind financially. This mostly matches views among all Texas voters.
And as is the case with voters overall, there is an enthusiasm gap, as more Hispanic Democrats than Hispanic Republicans are interested and motivated to vote in the midterms.
Overall, Hispanic voters prefer Talarico by 18 points (59% vs. 41%).
Some 9% of Hispanic GOP voters crossover to support Talarico while 5% of Hispanic Democrats favor Paxton.
CLICK HERE FOR CROSSTABS AND TOPLINE
In 2024, Trump topped former Vice President Kamala Harris among Hispanic voters in Texas by 1 point, according to the Texas FNVA survey (49% Harris vs. 50% Trump).
By 20 points, more Hispanic voters are concerned that Paxton lacks the character to serve as senator than feel Talarico is too extreme (61% concerned vs. 41%).
For the governor’s race, Hispanic voters back Hinojosa by 16 points in the new survey. By comparison, they preferred Beto O’Rourke over Abbott by 14 points in 2022.

More than half of Hispanic voters view Talarico (57% favorable), Hinojosa (53%), and the Democratic Party (53%) positively, while more than half have negative views of Paxton (56% unfavorable), Abbott (56%), Trump (61%), and the Republican Party (59%).

Conducted July 23-27, 2026, under the direction of Beacon Research (D) and Shaw & Company Research (R), this Fox News survey includes interviews with a sample of 1,006 Texas registered voters randomly selected from a statewide voter file. Respondents spoke with live interviewers on landlines (72) and cellphones (681) or completed the survey online after receiving a text (253). Results based on the full sample have a margin of sampling error of ±3 percentage points.

The survey includes an oversample of 296 Hispanic voters, bringing the sample size for that subgroup to 556 (±4). Sampling error for results among subgroups is higher. In addition to sampling errors, question wording and order can influence results. Weights are generally applied to age, race, education and area variables to ensure the demographics are representative of the registered voter population. Sources for developing weight targets include the most recent American Community Survey, Fox News Voter Analysis and voter file data.

title: 'The irony': Ketanji Brown Jackson roasted after stressing impartiality on Michelle Obama's podcast
summary: Ketanji Brown Jackson told Michelle Obama's "IMO" podcast she is "very, very mindful" of impartiality, sparking swift mockery over the perceived irony.
story: Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson agreed with former first lady Michelle Obama’s criticism of elite schools isolating students of color and recalled finding

Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson is being mocked online over the "irony" of saying she is "very, very mindful and scrupulous" about being impartial during a guest appearance on former first lady Michelle Obama’s podcast, "IMO."
During an appearance of more than an hour on the podcast, Jackson, a Biden appointee to the Supreme Court, stressed the importance of being unbiased, saying, "You really have to be focused on that."

"There are lots of limits on what judges can do, and I try to be very, very mindful and scrupulous with respect to that because, as you say, our obligation is to be unbiased in our approach," said Jackson.
MICHELLE OBAMA ACCUSES MEDIA OF WEAPONIZING FASHION TO 'DIMINISH' HER AS A CAMPAIGN THREAT
"And, so, you have to then navigate all the sources that could make for an appearance of partiality, which you want to avoid."
She added that "there are lots of things that I end up not accepting for that reason."

Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, left, recently appeared on a podcast episode hosted by former first lady Michelle Obama, right. (Emma McIntyre/Getty Images for The Recording Academy; Kent Nishimura/AFP via Getty Images)
The former first lady asked Jackson about the practices she follows to remain unbiased.

"You also have to watch your exposure to things, so that there isn’t a bias," said Obama. "What does that mean for you in terms of reading the paper and listening to the news? And how do get your information and what do you have to be careful about? And how are you dealing with the potential conflicts so that you do stay above board?"
SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER
Jackson said there are employees in the court whose job is to be "assisting us in that way."

"When I get invitations to do things, I always have them screened by the legal office, the public information office, just to make sure that there are no ethical conflicts, that this is not a fundraiser, you know," she told Obama.
ALITO RIPS JACKSON’S ‘UTTERLY IRRESPONSIBLE’ SOLO DISSENT AS SUPREME COURT FIGHT SHAKES UP 2026 MAP

Michelle Obama speaks at "IMO Live: Michelle Obama, Craig Robinson & Dr. Laurie Santos" during the SXSW Conference and Festivals at the Austin Convention Center in Austin, Texas, March 13, 2025. (Andy Wenstrand/SXSW Conference & Festivals)
Reactions poured in quickly.
"Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown discusses the importance of being neutral while she is sitting on Michelle Obama’s podcast set!" Turning Point USA contributor John Amanchukwu wrote.
"She doesn’t really expect anyone to believe that, does she?" conservative influencer Patricia Foster wrote.
"Make it make sense," commentator DeVory Darkins wrote.

"Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson can't be real. She says it is important to be neutral as a Supreme Court justice........while she is literally on MAJOR leftist Michelle Obama's podcast," Darkins wrote. "We ALL know how impartial she is."
'WOKE' SMITHSONIAN EXHIBIT LIONIZES EMBATTLED FAUCI AMID CONSERVATIVE SCRUTINY OF MUSEUM'S MESSAGING
Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson on the cover of Essence Magazine. (Essence Magazine)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Harris Rigby, a columnist for the Babylon Bee's non-satirical site "Not the Bee," wrote, "There isn't a strong enough word for the irony in this video clip."
He ripped Jackson as "the most public, loud-mouthed, self-assured judge in the history of the United States," adding that she now "wants to lecture us about the dignity of the courts."
Fox News Digital reached out to Obama and the Supreme Court for comment.
Peter Pinedo is a politics writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Trump promotes Freedom Haulers Initiative to fast-track military veterans into trucking jobs
summary: President Trump's Freedom Haulers Initiative streamlines CDL licensing for military veterans while removing over 24,000 non-English-speaking commercial drivers.
story: Program streamlines CDL licensing for veterans with military driving experience as administration touts crackdown on illegal immigrant commercial drivers.

President Donald Trump on Thursday formally kicked off an administration initiative designed to fast-track military veterans into trucking jobs while removing illegal immigrant commercial drivers from America's roadways, arguing the effort will improve highway safety and create new employment opportunities for former service members.

Speaking at the White House alongside Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, Veterans Affairs Secretary Doug Collins and trucking industry leaders, Trump promoted the "Freedom Haulers Initiative," which streamlines the commercial driver's license (CDL) process for veterans with heavy vehicle experience gained during military service.
"Today, we're taking action to get illegal alien truck drivers off the American roadways and replace them with proud American veterans," Trump said. "It's about time."
TRUMP TAPS VETERANS TO FIX ILLEGAL ALIEN TRUCKING PROBLEM PLAGUING US ROADWAYS

President Donald Trump speaks during an event promoting the Freedom Haulers Initiative at the White House, alongside Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, left, and Veterans Affairs Secretary Doug Collins, on July 30, 2026. (Peter D'Abrosca/Fox News Digital)

Under the initiative, qualified veterans with heavy-vehicle experience gained during military service can apply to waive the CDL road-skills test, allowing them to avoid duplicating training they received in the military. Certain veterans in participating states may also qualify for a waiver of the written knowledge test. Veterans without military truck-driving experience will be eligible for expedited training that administration officials said could be completed in several weeks.

Trump said 34 states have joined or are working to implement the Even Exchange Program, including Indiana, Wyoming, Louisiana, Arkansas, Alabama, Florida and Maryland, and called on the remaining states to participate.

The president paired the promotion with his administration's ongoing crackdown on commercial drivers who do not meet federal English-language requirements or who were issued licenses while in the country illegally.
OUT OF CONTROL, UNQUALIFIED ILLEGAL ALIEN TRUCKERS ENDANGERING KIDS ON US ROADS, INSIDER WARNS: ‘JUST MADNESS’

Veterans, trucking industry representatives and administration officials attend a White House event announcing the Trump administration's Freedom Haulers Initiative. (Peter D'Abrosca/Fox News Digital)

Trump said the administration has removed more than 24,000 non-English-speaking commercial drivers from behind the wheel and worked with states to cancel more than 28,000 commercial driver's licenses he said were unlawfully issued to illegal immigrants. He also pointed to several fatal crashes allegedly involving illegal immigrants while arguing for the policy change.
Duffy said the initiative eliminates unnecessary barriers for veterans transitioning into civilian careers while prioritizing highway safety.
"These are great-paying jobs. They're anywhere from $80,000 to $100,000-plus a year," Duffy said. "…illegals are out. American patriots are in."
ILLEGAL TRUCKER CASES FUEL GOP PUSH TO CRACK DOWN ON CDL MILLS AS DEMS LARGELY SILENT
President Donald Trump delivers remarks during a White House event announcing the Freedom Haulers Initiative alongside Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. (Peter D'Abrosca/Fox News Digital)

Collins said the Department of Veterans Affairs will also expand access to CDL training by allowing eligible veterans to use GI Bill benefits and by accelerating enrollment in existing training programs.
"Let's put veterans in the seats, making jobs safer and better for all Americans," Collins said, noting that roughly one in 10 truck drivers nationwide already are veterans.

Werner Enterprises President Nathan Meisgeier announced his company will hire 1,400 veterans over the next year as part of the Freedom Haulers Initiative, calling military veterans a natural fit for the trucking industry.
"This administration's Freedom Haulers campaign will have a direct and powerful impact on our ability to bring even more veterans into our workforce," Meisgeier said.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy speaks as President Donald Trump listens during a White House event announcing the Freedom Haulers Initiative, which aims to expand trucking opportunities for military veterans. (Peter D'Abrosca/Fox News Digital)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Army veteran Ricky Washington, who transitioned into commercial trucking after serving for three decades in the Army and Army National Guard, said the profession offers former service members another opportunity to serve the country.

"The trucking industry is more than just a sector of our economy — it's the backbone of our commerce," Washington said. "It is a place where service members, veterans [and] military spouses can find a purpose, a community and a way to continue keeping our great nation moving forward."
Peter D'Abrosca is a politics reporter at Fox News Digital.

title: House panel demands classified briefings on noncitizen voting, alleged Chinese election interference
summary: Rep. Bryan Steil demands classified DHS briefings on noncitizen voting and cyber vulnerabilities in voting systems ahead of November midterms.
story: A "Fox News Sunday" panel examines the controversy surrounding non-citizens found on New Jersey's voter rolls, with over 400 reported to have cast ballots.
The House committee charged with overseeing American elections is demanding more information on allegations of noncitizens voting in federal races.

The Committee on House Administration is requesting classified briefings on foreign interference in U.S. elections after President Donald Trump raised such concerns during a speech earlier this month.
"Reports of noncitizens casting illegal ballots continue to emerge, undermining election integrity and public confidence in American elections," wrote Committee Chairman Bryan Steil, R-Wis.

"To inform potential legislative reforms, the Committee therefore requests a Member-level, classified briefing from DHS on the number of non-citizens registered to vote across the country and cyber vulnerabilities present in current voting systems. Please contact the Committee by August 13, 2026, to set up a briefing to be held in the month of September. The Committee also requests that any relevant documents be provided alongside the briefing."
HOUSE REPUBLICANS CONFRONT NJ GOVERNOR OVER 6,600 NON-CITIZENS REGISTERED TO VOTE IN ALLEGED SOFTWARE FAILURE
Inside the Fairfax Government Center in Fairfax, Va., a voter is seen at a polling station during a referendum on redistricting. (Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP Photo)
The classified briefing requests were sent to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin, FBI Director Kash Patel and acting Director of National Intelligence (DNI) Bill Pulte.

In the letters, Steil cited Trump's claim that DHS discovered roughly 278,000 noncitizens registered to vote as well as recent revelations that New Jersey mistakenly added 6,600 noncitizens to its voter rolls in 2023 and 2024.
TRUMP ACCUSED CHINA OF AN 'ELECTION SECURITY NIGHTMARE' BUT THEN UNDERCUT HIS OWN WARNING
Steil also pointed to Trump's comments in his speech on Chinese-led "cyberattacks on election infrastructure."
President Donald Trump during a primetime address to the nation in the East Room of the White House in Washington, D.C., on July 16, 2026. (Saul Loeb/AFP/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
The committee's release said there were "serious concerns about the security of American elections."

The briefing requests come less than 100 days before the November midterm elections, which will decide which party controls both houses of Congress for the latter half of Trump's final term in the Oval Office.
Republicans have long raised concerns about the security of American elections, which Democrats have argued are attempts to undermine people's faith in those elections.
House Administration Committee Chairman Bryan Steil, R-Wis., holds a press conference in Washington, D.C., on Oct. 10, 2025. (Anna Rose Layden/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

It is already a federal crime to vote in elections as a noncitizen, but the GOP is pushing for further guardrails such as proof of citizenship in the voter registration process and a federal voter ID standard at the polls.
To date, no evidence has been found that noncitizens have swayed the outcome of any federal election.
Elizabeth Elkind is a politics reporter for Fox News Digital leading coverage of the House of Representatives. Previous digital bylines seen at Daily Mail and CBS News.
Follow on Twitter at @liz_elkind and send tips to elizabeth.elkind@fox.com

title: Dem senator swipes credit for bill he opposed amid heated re-election bid: 'Disturbing pattern'
summary: Jon Ossoff touted Georgia military construction wins at Fort Benning and Fort Stewart despite voting against the bill that funded those improvements.
story: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth testified before the Senate, defending the administration's $1.5 trillion budget request as a ‘generational investment’ crucial for military readiness and troop welfare.
Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., is touting his advocacy for federal investment in Georgia military infrastructure despite having ultimately voted against the bill that secured the improvements.

Most recently, Ossoff highlighted new construction for an elementary school at Fort Benning, improved conditions at Fort Stewart, pay raises for military personnel and improvements to Georgia’s foster care system — all a part of the annual military funding bill known as Military Construction and Veteran Affairs (MilCon-VA).
At the time of its initial passage, Ossoff quickly released a press statement.
FOX NEWS POLL: AN EARLY LOOK AT THE GEORGIA SENATE RACE
Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., speaks at a campaign event for President Joe Biden at Pullman Yards March 9, 2024, in Atlanta, Ga. (Megan Varner/Getty Images)
"U.S. Senate passes Sen. Ossoff’s Bipartisan Bill that provides most funding for Georgia military construction in 15 years," his website announced.
When reconsidering it for final passage, Ossoff opposed the package.

Notably, Ossoff, as the ranking member on the Senate Subcommittee on Military Construction and Veteran Affairs, voted in favor of the bill in committee and as a standalone bill but opposed its final passage later that year when it was bundled together with other government funding legislation.
When asked about the voting record, his office reaffirmed the federal support secured in Georgia.

"Let's be clear: Georgia's massive 2026 military construction budget, the highest in 15 years, is a direct and undeniable result of Senator Ossoff's work as the senior Democrat on the Military Construction subcommittee," an Ossoff campaign spokesperson told Fox News Digital in a statement.

"Senator Ossoff makes no apology for having tried to stop Mike Collins from doubling premiums for more than a million Georgians and throwing 300,000 off their health insurance," the spokesperson added.
The spokesperson was referring to Ossoff's Republican challenger, Rep. Mike Collins, R-Ga., and caps on federal health subsidies Republicans had championed at the time of MilCon-VA's passage.

Like many Democrats, Ossoff has struggled to oppose legislation championed by President Donald Trump while at the same time making his case for re-election in one of the country’s most competitive Senate seats. Ossoff won in 2021 with a 50.6% to 49.4% victory over incumbent Sen. David Perdue, R-Ga.
In the case of the elementary school, Ossoff said he had been calling for those investments for years.

"I have been working for years now for a replacement for Dexter Elementary. That’s really important for those families down there in Columbus," Ossoff said. "I’m just a bit concerned by the lack of attention in this year’s base budget, so we’ll work together on that."

Ossoff made similar remarks about improvements to Fort Stewart, citing concerns in press releases about lead exposure affecting newborns' health on the base, mold contamination and flooded living areas.
Ossoff released findings in a seven-page report about the base’s conditions.
SEN BLUMENTHAL, REP. TAKANO: CONGRESS CAN FUND VETERANS’ CARE WITHOUT TAKING BENEFITS FROM DISABLED HEROES
Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., speaks during an interview at Dobbins Air Reserve Base April 26, 2025, in Marietta, Ga. (AP)

"Our military service members and their families make huge sacrifices for the country, and it’s a travesty how they’re being treated by privatized housing contractors in Georgia and nationwide," Sen. Ossoff said.
"The stories in this report should shock our conscience, and I will continue exposing the mistreatment of military families in privatized housing and working to protect them and improve conditions."
Notably, the package Ossoff ultimately voted against contained $8 million for Fort Stewart and $127.4 million to replace the Dexter Elementary School.
A veteran lawmaker ripped Ossoff for highlighting wins he didn’t participate in.

"Last year, he tried to take credit for my veterans housing bill, legislation he had absolutely nothing to do with. A politician who tries to erase a veteran’s work for political gain has forfeited the trust of the people he seeks to represent," Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Wis., said in a statement, referring to a bill he introduced last year.

Ossoff highlighted the bill on his website, calling it a "bipartisan bill backed by U.S. Senator Jon Ossoff" and announcing that "Sen. Ossoff brings Republicans and Democrats together to protect veterans from foreclosure."
Ossoff was not a sponsor of the bill and, because it passed unanimously in a voice vote, did not cast a vote for it either.
