summary: Fabien Frankel talks his character Criston Cole meeting his bloody demise in “The Butcher’s Ball” on TODAY.
story: Warning: This post contains spoilers for “House of the Dragon.”
Fabien Frankel’s Criston Cole fulfilled his wish of dying “the realm’s greatest warrior” when met his bloody demise in “House of the Dragon.”
Minutes into Season 3, Episode 6 of “House of the Dragon,” entitled “The Butcher’s Ball,” Ser Cole led his men onto a battlefield that he thought was filled with deceased soldiers.

But his enemies were simply tricking him and arose, launching a sudden attack. Although Cole begged for his life and tried to surrender, his pleas were ignored and he died after being hit by multiple arrows.

It was an honorable death for Cole, and one he didn’t fear. In the episode prior, he said in a monologue, “I have been a servant all my life, to Green or to Black. I have defined myself by oaths, through unyielding devotion. And the highborn have made much of me while it pleased them to do so. But I will not let them diminish me now. I will not return spurned, rejected. I am the realm’s greatest warrior. And I will die as such.”
During an appearance on TODAY July 29, Frankel opened up about his character’s death.

“I knew I had it coming. I’d done so much bad stuff. I knew at some point I’d get a call saying our time was up. I lived a life. I did a lot of episodes. It was a good, long journey,” Frankel said on TODAY.
Frankel said he would “do a bit” with his friends about coming back for the show’s next season, even though his character’s fate was clearly spelled out in the book that inspired the show.

“I kept doing a while bit where I’d say, ‘I gotta go back next year, do a whole new season of the show.’ My friends were like, ‘You’re really lying directly to my face,’” he said. “I feel that’s apt for Criston and apt for myself.”
Frankel also described the “outpouring” he’s witnessed since his character’s death.
“There’s more love for Criston now than I felt ... now that he’s not alive, people maybe feel a little bit worse about hating him so much,” he said with a smile.
Cole, a divisive character, had appeared on the fantasy series since it premiered in 2022.

A day after the death of his character aired, Frankel posted a tribute to Cole on Instagram. Beside a carousel of behind-the-scenes photos taken on the set of the HBO series, Frankel wrote in the caption, “3 seasons. 21 episodes. 5 and half years. A badly dealt with heartbreak.”
He added, “To all of you who tuned in every week, And to all those who have carried me along the way, I couldn’t have gotten through it without you. It’s been an honour. Criston Cole, over and out.”
Fans complimented Frankel’s performance on the show in the comments.
“Hated your character which means you are a spectacular actor sir,” one said.
Another agreed and wrote, “A sign of a great actor is that they can make you hate them on screen. You were up there with some of the most hated in the GoT universe and we love you for that!”
The official HBO account also left a message that read, “We thank you for your valiant service to the crown, Ser Fabien.”

title: Oscar-Winning Irish Singer-Songwriter Glen Hansard Dies in Dublin Motorcycle Crash
summary: Academy Award-winning Irish singer-songwriter Glen Hansard died in a motorcycle crash in Dublin early Wednesday, his management said.
story: Academy Award-winning Irish singer-songwriter Glen Hansard died in a motorcycle crash in Dublin early Wednesday, his management said. He was 56.
ATC Management told broadcaster RTE Hansard’s family was “deeply shocked and heartbroken” by his death.

Irish police said a man in his 50s died in single vehicle motorcycle crash in Lucan on the outskirts of the Irish capital before 4:30 a.m. on Wednesday. The man, who they did not name, was treated at the scene but was pronounced dead a short time later.

Hansard combined acting and a musical career. He played a member of a Dublin soul band in 1991 movie “The Commitments” and won an Oscar in 2008 for the song “Falling Slowly” from the film “Once,” in which he starred alongside Markéta Irglová.

He was long-serving front man for rock band The Frames, half of rock duo The Swell Season and released solo albums including “Didn’t He Ramble,” which was nominated for a Grammy for Best Folk Album in 2016.
For years, Hansard led the Christmas Eve charity busk outside Dublin’s Gaiety Theatre, where members of the public gathered to see famous Irish musicians perform in aid of the Dublin Simon Community.

At the funeral of The Pogues frontman Shane MacGowan in 2023, Hansard performed The Pogues’ song “Fairytale Of New York” with Irish singer Lisa O’Neill, which prompted dancing in the aisles of the church.
Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin said he was “deeply saddened to learn of the passing of Glen Hansard.”
“A talented musician and actor who made a significant contribution to Ireland’s cultural landscape over many years,” Martin posted on X.

title: Karlie Kloss Calls Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce an ‘Amazing Couple’ After Going to Their Wedding: EXCLUSIVE
summary: Karlie Kloss opened up to TODAY about her new book and said that Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are an “amazing couple.’
story: Weeks after being photographed heading to Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce’s wedding in New York, Karlie Kloss opened up about the nuptials.

“Listen, I try to protect the privacy of my friends’ personal lives,” Kloss said during an appearance on TODAY on July 28. “But what I will say is that they’re an amazing couple and I’m so happy for them.”

Swift and Kelce’s wedding unfolded on July 3 in New York, drawing a star-studded crowd to Madison Square Garden. While most of the wedding has been kept secret, guests have shared a few details, like handkerchiefs embroidered with a T&T logo and who, exactly, caught the bouquet.

Kloss and Swift met at a fashion show in 2013, Swift confirmed to Vogue in 2015, and became fast friends. The two shared bits of their friendship with the world and the press. Kloss even appeared in Swift’s “Bad Blood” music video in 2015.

However, the two have not been photographed or seen together publicly since 2016. Swift did not attend either of Kloss’ wedding ceremonies to Joshua Kushner in 2018 and 2019. Of their friendship, a 2018 New York Times profile of Kloss said, “Despite internet gossip suggesting otherwise, the pair continues to be good friends and they talk frequently.”

Kloss, meanwhile, is interested in untangling a different type of problem. Over a decade ago, the former supermodel started a non-profit technology education program, Kode With Klossy, a camp that connects young girls with opportunities and support in the technology and computer science space.
Her first children’s book, “Spaghetti Code: A Story About Problem-Solving, Pasta, and the Power of Big Ideas,” out July 28, introduces coding concepts to 4 to 8-year-olds.

“‘Spaghetti code’ is a term that means when your code is a hot mess. There’s a bug in there somewhere and you’ve got to fix it,” Kloss said on TODAY. “The idea is to not get frustrated or overwhelmed when you hit a mistake, but to work through it and keep going.”
The mom of three called her leap into writing a children’s picture book about coding principles a “tall order,” but wanted it to be “really fun and visual.”
“‘Spaghetti Code’ is really inspired by our scholars, who are these incredible, passionate young women from around the world,” Kloss said.
“Spaghetti Code” is the first in a five-book series, per Publisher’s Weekly.

title: John Mulaney Announces 9 New York City Shows: EXCLUSIVE
summary: John Mulaney has revealed he will perform at nine New York City venues over nine straight days, ending with a performance at Madison Square Garden.
story: He’s already conquered the Windy City — now John Mulaney has his eyes set on the Big Apple.

Mulaney, who became the first comedian to headline Chicago’s Wrigley Field during a July 11 show, has announced “Mulaney Takes Manhattan,” a series of nine shows over nine days in New York City, culminating with a performance at Madison Square Garden, he revealed exclusively on TODAY on July 28.

“Instead of doing one show in New York City, or even three shows in New York City, for my tour, I’m going to do a very special run. Nine different iconic New York City venues in nine nights,” he said.

“This is very, very cool, I must say. I’m doing something very cool, and I’m a very cool person,” he joked. “This is really a great way to do the intimate small places. I love playing here, building up to Madison Square Garden, doing Radio City (Music Hall). I filmed a special at Radio City, to go back there. It’s going to be really cool.”
The shows, which will begin Jan. 7, 2027 and end Jan. 15, 2027, will feature special guests and a new experience each performance.
You can sign up for a chance to get tickets at johnmulaney.com.
Here’s a look at all of the shows.

Thursday, Jan. 7 — Comedy CellarFriday, Jan. 8 — Blue Note Saturday, Jan. 9 — Joe’s PubSunday, Jan. 10 — Bowery BallroomMonday, Jan. 11 — Music Box Theater on Broadway Tuesday, Jan. 12 — Beacon TheatreWednesday, Jan. 13 — Carnegie HallThursday, Jan. 14 — Radio City Music HallFriday, Jan. 15 — Madison Square Garden
Thursday, Jan. 7 — Comedy Cellar
Friday, Jan. 8 — Blue Note
Saturday, Jan. 9 — Joe’s Pub
Sunday, Jan. 10 — Bowery Ballroom
Monday, Jan. 11 — Music Box Theater on Broadway
Tuesday, Jan. 12 — Beacon Theatre
Wednesday, Jan. 13 — Carnegie Hall
Thursday, Jan. 14 — Radio City Music Hall
Friday, Jan. 15 — Madison Square Garden
Mulaney is in the middle of his “Mister Whatever Tour,” which stopped at Wrigley Field — home of the Chicago Cubs — for his history-making performance.
“It was iconic. It might’ve been too big,” he said.
“It was like playing a spaceship. And who brought me up, but Mr. David Letterman,” he added, as video of the legendary comedian introducing him played, a moment that left him in awe.
“What’s cool about something that crazy is you don’t even have to put it in perspective. It was just wild. And then the show itself was like flying a spaceship,” he said.

title: ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’ Ends With Surprising Elimination After Contestant Gets Injured
summary: Another contestant has been eliminated on “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro.” The third episode saw one dancer leave the ballroom after group challeneges.
story: There’s no room for mistakes as the competition continues on “Dancing With the Stars: The Next Pro.”
With nine dancers remaining, Episode 3 of the “Dancing With the Stars” spinoff is challenging the contestants with group performances.

“DWTS” pro Britt Stewart joined judges Shirley and Mark Ballas during the Monday, July 27, episode. The dancer helped mentor the contestants as they took on high-intensity routines that they had to learn and master in just hours.
Group performances are key to opening a “DWTS” live show and entertaining the audiences. They also test the individuals on teamwork, taking direction, giving feedback and timing.
So, how did the contestants fare?
What Happened During Episode 3 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’
Britt entered the ballroom performing a dynamic group tango that impressed all. Host Robert Irwin then revealed that the dancers’ first challenge would be to re-create Britt’s exact choreography.

Then it was time for rehearsals, where the nine contestants learned the steps and took direction from Britt. Some felt they excelled in group performances, while others faced difficulties being in sync, spacing and picking up the choreography.

However, in one unexpected moment Natalie Jolley was accidentally hit in the eye by Stephani Sosa. Natalie was transported to the hospital to receive medical attention, which meant the group was down by one.

The show had to continue and after just three hours of rehearsals, Britt informed the crew that it was time to perform for the judges. She said that was the amount of time “DWTS” pros had to learn opening numbers and be camera ready.

The performance had its hits and misses, with the judges determining that Tristan Sanders and Nina Mayster were the weakest links. But, they were not on the chopping block just yet. Britt informed them that they would have another chance to prove their skills in the second group challenge.

Given a chance to redeem themselves, Tristan, who became emotional following feedback, and Nina were then chosen to be the team captains in the second challenge. The two had to select who they wanted on their teams to create and perform another group dance. Meanwhile, Natalie was under “medical supervision” and could not participate.
On Nina’s team were Allen Genkin, AJ Pritchard and Adele Zaikman. They had to perform a tango.
Tristan chose Stephani, Selena Hamilton and Erik Linder. They would be performing a paso doble.
Both teams faced their own obstacles during rehearsals and when it was showtime, one group outshined the other.
Tristan’s team was up first, with judges noting that despite their dynamic and powerful opening, they were dancing as individuals and not as a group.

When it came to Nina’s team, Allen fumbled and fell but quickly got up and kept going. Mark did call him out yet applauded his efforts in not letting it affect the rest of the routine. He also praised Nina for letting someone else take the lead after she was told that she tried to take control in past episodes. All three judges agreed that it was visible that they were able to put their egos aside and work together.
Who Was in the Bottom 2?
The group that impressed the judges most due to their synchronicity and teamwork was Nina’s team. They were safe from elimination.
Unfortunately, Tristan’s team was in jeopardy and two dancers were up for elimination. Due to their mistakes, Selena and Tristan were in the bottom two.
Who Got Eliminated on Episode 3 of ‘DWTS: The Next Pro’?

Fortunately, because of Natalie’s injury, she was not medically cleared to continue competing in the show. This meant that she was automatically eliminated and Tristan and Selena were safe for another week.
Natalie returned to the ballroom to say she was “sad and disappointed” that she wouldn’t be able to continue in the competition. She understood that at this time she had to take care of her health.
What Will Happen Next Week?
Eight contestants remain in the competition. The next episode of “DWTS: The Next Pro” will air on Aug. 3.

Guest mentor and “DWTS” champ Jenna Johnson will help the remaining  dancers work on their chemistry and bring the heat and passion into their routines. The lowest-scoring pair will then be eliminated.

title: Here’s When ‘Michael’ Will Start Streaming
summary: Fans will soon get to experience Jafaar Jackson’s transformation into Michael Jackson in “Michael” over and over again when the film starts streaming. Find out how to watch.
story: Fans will soon get to experience Jafaar Jackson’s transformation into Michael Jackson in the hit biopic “Michael” over and over again when the film starts streaming.

On July 27, Starz announced in a press release that the blockbuster film about the King of Pop will make its streaming debut on its platform. The move to streaming comes after “Michael,” which hit theaters in April, had a successful and lengthy run at the box office. The movie earned $1 billion globally and became the highest-grossing biopic of all time, according to the press release, with the late icon’s fans flocking to theaters to see pivotal moments of his life on the big screen.

“Michael” begins with a young Michael, played by Juliano Valdi, growing up in Gary, Indiana, with demanding father Joe Jackson, portrayed by Colman Domingo. Michael becomes a household name as a child before a time jump finds the legend, now played by real-life nephew Jafaar Jackson, eager to embark on a solo career and embrace a new sound.

The film features re-creations of the singer’s iconic looks, as well as many highlights from the Grammy winner’s career, such as the filming of his “Thriller” music video and the “Victory Tour” with his brothers. The movie touches on some low points in his life, too, like his relationship with his father and the moment he was burned while filming a Pepsi commercial.
The film also stars Nia Long, Miles Teller, Laura Harrier, Kendrick Sampson and Mike Meyers.
While the flick was panned by critics and has a 38% on Rotten Tomatoes, the audience score was much more favorable at 97%.
Find out how and when to stream “Michael” from the comfort of your couch, below.
How to Watch ‘Michael’ at Home
“Michael will be available to stream exclusively on Starz. Fans will be able to watch the film using the Starz app and all Starz streaming and on-demand platforms.
When to Stream ‘Michael’ at Home
The movie will stream for the first time starting on Monday, Aug. 10.
Additionally, “Michael” will make its television premiere on the Starz channel the same day at 7 p.m. ET/PT.

title: Emily Wilson’s ‘Odyssey’ Translation Inspired the New Movie. Her Review Is Scathing
summary: What “Odyssey” translator and classicist Emily wrote about Christopher Nolan’s movie in her review.
story: Classicist and translator Emily Wilson has some thoughts on Christopher Nolan’s latest blockbuster, “The Odyssey,” calling out the film’s lack of “narrative and emotional depth,” its depiction of the female characters and the misunderstanding of its themes, among many other criticisms.

“The Odyssey,” which hit theaters July 17 and stars Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Tom Holland, Zendaya and more famous faces, has received overwhelming praise from fans and critics alike.

The epic, an adaptation of Homer’s ancient Greek poem, has landed at the top of the box office for the last two weeks, already bringing in over $280 million domestically and nearly $640 million worldwide, according to Box Office Mojo. The fantasy flick also debuted with a 98% score on Rotten Tomatoes from critics and has a 97% audience rating as of July 27.
But some classics professors have voiced their issues with the film, most notably Wilson, whose translation of “The Odyssey” influenced Nolan.
Before the film’s release, the auteur quoted Wilson’s translation in a November 2025 interview with Empire.

“I think it’s the Emily Wilson translation that begins, ‘Tell me about a complicated man’,” Nolan said at the time. “The genius of the character, the cleverness, the inventiveness of him, that was a huge part of what interested me. He’s not just a soldier. He’s an amazing strategist, a very wily person.”
After seeing the film, Wilson penned a review for the London Review of Books, which she titled “An Uncomplicated Man.”

In the lengthy critique, Wilson broke down all the areas in which she argues the film fell short, writing that although she was “humbled” when she read Nolan was familiar with her translation, she would have been “ashamed to have written any part of this script.”
Wilson began her review by complimenting Nolan’s version of “The Odyssey” for not being boring.

But she credits that to the strength of the source material. She describes the Oscar-winner’s imagining as “family-friendly audiovisual spectacle, like an elaborate Fourth of July fireworks display — and with about the same level of narrative and emotional depth.”

She noted a pattern of “grandiosity and superficiality” she has seen in some of the director’s past works and similarities particularly in the action-packed sequences. Wilson then mentioned multiple scenes in the movie that she said didn’t elicit an expected emotional reaction, such as the moment Odysseus and his crew sail past the Sirens.
She also said the film is less focused on developing its characters but succeeds “at conveying big bangs and big giants.”
That appears to be the crux of her criticism: the epic tries to do too much.
She wrote, “There is no restraint in Nolan’s version of ‘The Odyssey’: every second is jam-packed with incident, lights and noise, and nothing is ever at a human scale.”
However, one creative choice she didn’t mind was the movie’s the use of American accents and modern contemporary language.

“Despite the manufactured online outrage, there is nothing inherently wrong with the movie’s attempt to approximate contemporary American speech,” she said. “If you’re not going to compose a script in Homeric Greek, or even in metrical English verse, you might as well use something like conversational American English.”
But that doesn’t mean she was a fan of how the choice was executed.
“The language is relentlessly expository, humourless and flat,” Wilson added.
While she applauded some performances, like Hathaway as Penelope and Samantha Morton’s Circe, she said that none of the female characters were portrayed as well as they were written in Homer’s poem.
In summary, “The writing is abysmal. None of the characters has convincing motivation for their actions or words. There are no sex scenes, and all the food looks horrible,” she said.

Although she found the film’s message to be murky, she ended her review explaining why she is still “grateful” the movie was made. She pointed out “The Odyssey”’s worldwide success in a streaming era and how it is driving fans to read multiple translations of the original.

“Nolan, who studied English at University College London — where students still study ‘The Odyssey’ as a first year ‘foundational text’ — is doing his best to get the general public reading again, and I am grateful,” Wilson concludes.
Social media users reacted to her scathing review on X.
Many disagreed with her take, writing that “The Odyssey”’s themes and message about the effects of war were clear.
“I do think The Odyssey had quite a lot to say about war, actually,” one person tweeted.
Another said, “She’s so caught up in literal translations that she’s missing the broader point of a modern interpretation, which stops her from experiencing an excellent film.”
A third agreed that Wilson seemed unwilling to let go of the source material and immerse herself in the adaptation.

“All love to emily wilson who has a way different relationship with the odyssey than the rest of us but that critique is on some level her being unable to reconcile w the fact that this is ‘nolan’s odyssey’, not ‘nolan making homer’s odyssey into a motion picture,” the X user said.
Others shared Wilson’s point of view.
“I love how she defends Nolan’s right to make his own story out it as Homer itself is and then goes to town on what is actually made,” one praised. “This is a great critique piece.”
Another simply said, “Did i love the movie? yes. is emily wilson also correct? Yes.”

title: Keke Palmer Says She Has ‘Genuine Chemistry’ with Sean Evans: ‘Couldn’t Force That If I Tried’
summary: Keke Palmer talks with TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle about her “chemistry” with “Hot Ones” host Sean Evans.
story: Keke Palmer is setting the record straight on her relationship with “Hot Ones” host and co-creator Sean Evans.

The pair’s chemistry has sparked headlines for years. Evans was a guest on her “Baby, This is Keke Palmer” podcast in May, re-igniting conversation about their connection on social media. A few weeks later, they were spotted having dinner together.
“Our chemistry is genuine ... I couldn’t force that if I tried,” Palmer said July 27 on TODAY with Jenna & Sheinelle. “We always felt that chemistry.”
Things reached a fever pitch when the photo of them having dinner together made the rounds.
“It’s life. Essentially, we met at work. We had chemistry. Work husband, work wife. You just have that chemistry with people,” Palmer said of the dinner. “Then, we hang out.”
Palmer said the response to the photo, and to their perceived connection, has stunned her.
“I was gagged that everybody was ready to marry me off,” she said. “Guys, let it cook! They married your girl off in two seconds!”
In her words, fans “write the story quicker than you can live it.”
Palmer said there’s been no way to avoid the interest from the public.

“I see somebody at the airport. I’m going through TSA. They’re like, ‘So, girl, what’s going on?’” she said. “I’m like, ‘Well, girl, you gotta let time pass. This just happened yesterday.’ So it’s like this thing where, it’s so interesting. It’s so parasocial, the world we live in now.”
The “Nope” actor is not averse to avoiding the dialogue that may exist around her online.

“I do look sometimes, especially because, first of all, I love pop culture, and I like to know what’s going on,” she said. “For me, sometimes the internet can be similar to, that’s like when I’m waking up and I’m watching y’all on the news. It’s like sometimes you need to know, just so you can stay abreast.

“I don’t let it define the way that I think. If anything, I’m always trying to contextualize things. A lot times I feel like people get that about me. You can’t just take everything at face value. You have to be critically thinking about everything you see.”

Talk that Palmer and Evans were romantically involved began in November 2023 after he named Palmer when asked on Amelia Dimoldenberg’s “Chicken Shop Date” if he ever had a crush on a guest. At that point, Palmer had appeared on “Hot Ones” in 2017 and 2021.
Rumors swirled more after Palmer returned to his show in September 2025 and the two kissed.
Last month, Palmer spoke about the relationship while on the panel for Spotify’s Conversations That Channel Culture talk at Cannes Lions.
Podcast host Jay Shetty asked the actor if she was “serious about Sean Evans,” according to People.
“First of all, I love Sean Evans — I love Sean, hey Sean. That’s my guy ... You never know what can arise from there. We just take it day by day. One wing at a time, so to speak,” she added.

title: Carly Simon Reveals She’s Been Diagnosed with Parkinson’s Disease
summary: Carly Simon revealed to NBC News she has been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease and has also been treated for skin cancer.
story: Carly Simon has revealed she has Parkinson’s disease.
The Grammy-winning singer, 83, shared the news July 27 when providing an update on her health and explaining her absence from the public eye.

“So many people have written to me, kindly wondering about my relative silence, asking how I am and what I have been doing. The truth is, I’ve been learning how to live with Parkinson’s disease,” she said in a statement obtained by NBC News.

“It has taken me some time to understand the diagnosis, to adjust to it, and to decide how much I wanted to say about it publicly. Parkinson’s is different for everyone, and it can be unpredictable. Some days I’m so tired I can’t get the day moving at all. On others, it gives me a little more room to move, think, work, and feel like myself.”
Simon said her health challenges began with arthritis in her knees and one of her hips, which prompted joint replacement surgeries but didn’t solve her mobility problems.

“Eventually, there were periods when I could not walk without considerable help,” she said. “My family and I knew that something more was going on. After an extensive evaluation at the Mayo Clinic, I was diagnosed with Parkinson’s.”

The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame member began taking medication to help with her mobility and other symptoms. She also said that while Parkinson’s is thought of as primarily affecting movement, she’s also experienced “anxiety, depression, exhaustion, and apathy.”

“That has been one of the hardest things to explain,” she said. “It is not simply sadness or laziness. It is as though the part of the brain that sends out invitations to participate in life has temporarily misplaced the guest list.”
Simon then said she was treated for basal cell carcinoma on her face that was removed, “but the surgery affected my appearance and made me more self-conscious about being seen in public.”
She said her problems with movement, along with the Parkinson’s, her surgery and the emotional impact of what she was going through, she had decided to retreat from the spotlight.
“But I have not stopped living, and I have not stopped working,” she added, noting she has been recording a new album called “Comes in Waves” and that has provided her some relief.

“Working on the music gave shape to days that did not always have much shape,” she said. “It gave me somewhere to go without having to leave the room. It reminded me that illness can change your life without becoming the whole of your life.

“I do not consider Parkinson’s a gift or a blessing. It is neither. It is difficult, frustrating, and sometimes frightening. I am still learning how to live with it and how to accept it without feeling that I have surrendered something essential.”
Simon thanked all of those people who have helped through her journey.
“These days I move more slowly, I lean on others more than I once did, and I have learned to accept that every day will look a little different. But I am still very much here,” she said.
What Is Parkinson’s Disease?

Parkinson’s disease is a brain disorder that occurs when nerve cells in the area of the brain that controls movement, called the basal ganglia, stop functioning properly or die, according to the National Institute on Aging.

Hallmark symptoms include uncontrolled movements, like shaking and stiffness, as well as struggling with balance or coordination. As the disease progresses, it can harm one’s ability to walk and talk, and result in behavior changes, memory issues, problems sleeping, depression and more.

The disease is most commonly diagnosed in people 60 and over. There is no cure for Parkinson’s, although there are a variety of treatments to lessen symptoms. Doctors typically diagnose the disease by performing a neurological exam and taking a patient’s medical history.
What Type of Cancer Did Carly Simon Have?
The “You’re So Vain” singer shared in her recent health update that she underwent surgery to remove a basal cell carcinoma, a type of skin cancer, from her face.
“Basal cell carcinoma often looks like a slightly transparent bump on the skin, though it can take other forms,”  according to the Mayo Clinic.
It can also look like a brown, black or blue lesion; a scaly patch that grows over time; or a white scar-like lesion.
It most commonly occurs because of exposure to sunlight. Wearing sunscreen and reducing exposure to the sun can decrease the risk of developing basal cell carcinoma.

To prevent skin cancer, the Mayo Clinic recommends staying out of the sun in the middle of the day, applying sunscreen year-round, wearing clothing that covers arms and legs, not using tanning beds, and paying attention to new growths on skin, as well as changes to moles, freckles, bumps and birthmarks.
Simon was also diagnosed with breast cancer in 1997. She underwent surgery and chemotherapy.

Cancer runs in Simon’s family. Her two sisters died of cancer one day apart in 2022. Joanna Simon died of thyroid cancer, one day shy of her 86th birthday. Lucy Simon died of metastatic breast cancer at 82. In 2018, their brother, Peter, the youngest sibling, died of cardiac arrest at age 71, which occurred after he had been diagnosed with cancer.

title: The Internet Reacts to Raising Cane’s AI Chuck Norris Ads: ‘Dystopian’
summary: Social media users might be weirded out by Raising Cane’s AI depiction of Chuck Norris, but his family approves of the National Chicken Finger Day campaign.
story: Raising Cane’s newest spokesperson is not a person at all.

On July 14, the chicken chain announced it is donating $1 from every Box Combo sold on National Chicken Finger Day (July 27) up to $1 million to benefit Kickstart Kids, the martial arts youth development organization co-founded by Chuck Norris.
The actor, who was a close friend of Raising Cane’s founder Todd Graves, died in March at age 86.
For this charity drive, Raising Cane’s has depicted the “Walker Texas Ranger” star in print, video and more by using artificial intelligence — and people online have a lot to say about it.
“why is nobody talking about the fact raising canes is running ai ads,” asked an X user, posting a commercial where an AI Norris uses a disposable straw to dispatch with a henchman.
“Walked in and was dumbfounded by how bad it was,” wrote one Reddit user in a post titled, “Gross Generative AI Chuck Norris Signage.”
“Dystopian,” noted another.
“this actually breaks my heart and i should’ve expected this,” someone else wrote.
“Disgraceful tbh,” posted one more. “billionaire can’t pay an artist a decent wage. Embarrassing.”
A representative for Raising Cane’s tells TODAY.com that these ads were created with the encouragement and approval of the Norris family.
The nationwide campaign spans television, digital, social media, billboards and Raising Cane’s restaurants, and is led by a spot featuring Gena Norris and twins Dakota Norris and Danilee Norris.
In other ads, created with AI and supported by the Norris family, Graves himself teams up with the digitally rendered Chuck to protect their local Raising Cane’s from a siege of masked henchmen.
“Chuck and Todd shared a friendship built on mutual respect, generosity and a belief in helping young people become the best versions of themselves,” Gena Norris said in a press release.

“Chuck would be deeply honored to know that his legacy is continuing in such a meaningful way,” she continues. “Our family is incredibly grateful to Todd and everyone at Raising Cane’s for celebrating my husband’s life and helping carry forward the work that meant so much to him. We’re proud to be part of this campaign and know it will make a difference in the lives of kids across the country.”
In contrast, the family came out against AI-generated videos about the action star’s death in April.

“We are aware that since Chuck’s passing, there have been a number of AI-generated videos and posts circulating online that contain false and misleading information regarding the circumstances of his passing, his health history, and who was present,” read a statement posted to his Instagram stories, according to Variety.

“These claims are entirely untrue. This includes fabricated reports of past medical issues, as well as false narratives surrounding family relationships,” the statement continued. The family asked people to “not believe or share any information,” unless it comes directly from them or an “official family representative.”

While the Norris family didn’t specify which posts triggered their statement, one notable AI image that made the rounds depicted his funeral, attended by AI-generated versions of Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Jackie Chan, Bruce Willis, Dolph Lundgren and Mel Gibson.

title: Do You Really Need to See ‘The Odyssey’ in IMAX? What 70mm and Other Formats Mean
summary: Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” sparked a debate around its formats and the right way to view the movie. HEre’s what to know about IMAX, 70mm and more.
story: Christopher Nolan’s “The Odyssey” hit theaters July 17, and the struggle to secure IMAX tickets may be just as grueling as Odysseus’ 10-year journey across the Mediterranean and Aegean seas.
Nolan’s depiction of the Greek epic is the first feature film to be shot entirely on 70mm IMAX cameras.

Cinephiles will tell you this leads to an elevated viewing experience, but there is a supply-and-demand issue with finding screenings that support this special type of film. In an interview with Variety, IMAX CEO Richard Gelfond said 70mm IMAX theaters are sold out into the movie’s fifth week, including 2 a.m. and 7 a.m. screenings.
Casual moviegoers are wondering: What even is 70mm IMAX, and how much am I missing out if I can’t see it in the intended viewing format?
TODAY.com spoke to film industry experts to break down why watching “The Odyssey” has become an epic puzzle.
What, Exactly, Is 70mm IMAX?
70mm IMAX is a wide-resolution film allowing for a larger image quality than the typical 35mm film.
Film marketing professional Lia Baek says 70mm IMAX film “can deliver exceptionally high image detail and show more image vertically than most digital IMAX or standard screenings.”
While Nolan’s stylistic flair allows for an immersive, high-resolution viewing experience, there’s a catch: 70mm IMAX screenings are only available at 25 movie theaters in the U.S.

IMAX CEO Walter Gelfond told Variety the issue with making more IMAX 70mm theaters. “The problem is they haven’t made new IMAX film projectors in about 50 years. So we retrofit them, rebuild them and part of our strategy is to see how far we can take it. But certainly, demand-driven, I’d like to see more,” he said.

Walter Nicoletti, founder of Voce Spettacolo, a film production and distribution company, brings up the involved maintenance process and associated costs as a barrier as well. He says a single 70mm film strip requires a reel weighing over 500 pounds.
What’s the Difference Between 70mm IMAX and Regular IMAX?

70mm IMAX fills up even more of the screen than typical IMAX screenings, as demonstrated on the movie’s website. That’s because it presents films with a 1:43:1 aspect ratio, as opposed to regular IMAX’s 1:90:1.
“The IMAX experience can still be highly immersive, but it is not identical to an IMAX 70mm film presentation,” Baek explains.
There Are Other Formats to See ‘The Odyssey,’ Too
Aside from the intended 70mm IMAX experience and digital IMAX, there are still four other viewing formats viewers can choose from.
The film’s official website breaks down everything, including descriptions from the stars themselves.
Here are all of the options, explained:

“Each film frame has 15 perforations and runs horizontally through the projector. It is the largest and highest-resolution format available and gives you an unparalleled sense of immersion as the image fills IMAX’s signature floor-to-ceiling screen,” according to the website.
“When you’re in the theater, you’ll feel the full impact of how it was shot,” Matt Damon, who plays the titular Odysseus, explained.
Standard IMAX (1:90:1)
Standard IMAX (1:90:1)

“The film will be presented in IMAX’s 1.90:1 Expanded Aspect Ratio with select IMAX with Laser locations showing it in IMAX’S 1.43:1 Expanded Aspect Ratio. The film will fill your entire field of vision on the floor-to-ceiling screen,” the website says.

“The film was shot and designed to be experienced on the biggest screen possible, and IMAX delivers on this,” Anne Hathaway, who plays Penelope, explained in a video on the site. “It fills your entire field of vision, immersing you fully for the best cinematic experience.”

“70MM film is large format film that offers a bright, clear image up to 3 times the resolution of standard digital projection formats, with rich analog color by projecting light through celluloid. 70MM film has 5 perforations and runs vertically through the projector,” according to the website.
“There’s nothing like seeing a movie shot on film presented on film,” Lupita Nyong’o said in her video.
The website highlights this “classic film format” that “projects light through the entire 35 millimeter frame to deliver clear, high resolution images with rich analog color.”
In his video, Robert Pattinson, who plays Antinous, recommended this format for a “classic” experience exclusive to a movie theater atmosphere.
Dolby Vision
Dolby Vision
Zendaya called this format “an experience all its own.”
“Dolby’s dynamic range, brightness and color draws you in, giving you a vivid visual experience and what Christopher Nolan captured will be presented with impact.”
Premium Large Format
Premium Large Format
This format presents itself outside of the screen appearance in two ways: 4DX or D-BOX.
While both experiences involve vibrating seat movements, 4DX also includes corresponding weather and scent effects.
Tom Holland, who plays Telemachus, also highlighted the “wall-to-wall screens and superior projection technology.”
“If you want to feel the movie, see ‘The Odyssey’ in 4DX or D-Box,” Holland said.
Which Formats Do Film Experts Recommend?
Film professor Harry Marks shares his advice to anyone trying to decode each option.

“Nolan composed the film so nothing essential gets cropped across the other formats,” Marks says. “My honest guidance: see it on the best screen you can realistically get to, and don’t let the scarcity convince you that any other way is a failure.”
Standard digital screenings, such as 35mm and the Dolby and PLF, are “fully valid” according to Baek, but she says part of the image area is technically lost.
“They may not reproduce the complete image area, scale or physical film characteristics of the 70mm IMAX version,” she says.
Marks highlights that Dolby Vision offers extreme contrast and brightness, and, along with the PLF, they are by far the most available, and where most people will be able to see “The Odyssey.”
Why the Formats Have Started a Debate
There are a few aspects to the debate.
Online, people are pointing out that the movie looks different depending on the format you see it in — essentially, a portion of the image is cut off if you’re not seeing it in IMAX.
“Nolan did a disservice to the majority of viewers who don’t have access to IMAX,” one X user wrote, comparing images from two different showings.
Then, even if you can see it in IMAX, it’s hard to actually nab a ticket.
Experts say the debate and the demand shows that consumers are willing to see movies in theaters, despite at-home viewing rising during the pandemic.

“(Viewers are) willing to pay top dollar and travel long distances for an experience they can’t replicate on a OLED TV or smartphone,” Nicoletti says. “The format debate proves that people go to the theatre not just to see a plot, but they go for physical scale and amazing visual quality.”

title: ‘Love Island USA’ Star Nic Vansteenberghe Addresses Split from Olandria Carthen
summary: “Love Island USA” couple Olandria Carthen and Nic Vansteenberghe have broken up, Nic confirmed in a TikTok post.
story: “Love Island USA’s” Olandria Carthen and Nic Vansteenberghe — better known to their fans as Nicolandria — have called it quits.
Nic, 25, confirmed the news in a post to his TikTok subscribers July 26. The separation comes roughly a year after they were named runners-up last summer on Season 7 of the reality dating show.

“To Nicolandria community,” Nic wrote. “The rumors are true. I didn’t want to Give people false hope, so I wanted To clear the air. We will continue To love each other ALWAYS. It’s a sensitive, as well as a private Subject, thank you for respecting Our privacy.”

Olandria and Nic took a nontraditional path to one another on “Love Island USA.” The pair, whose season premiered June 3, 2025, were initially coupled up with other people; Olandria with Taylor Williams and Nic with Cierra Ortega. However, during the show’s infamous Casa Amor episode, the two were both dumped, only to be spared and coupled up together, allowing them both to return to the villa.

Sparks didn’t fly during their first coupling, and the two decided to pursue their initial connections. However, Cierra ended up being cut from the show due to controversy around her previous use of a racial slur. Olandria and Nic gave things another go, just days before the show’s finale, quickly becoming a favorite in the eyes of the show’s loyal fans.

Since leaving the island, both “Love Island USA” contestants experienced an uptick in fame, with the two appearing in a flurry of promotions together, including spots for swimwear, makeup and more. However, the two remained vague when it came to defining their relationship. While at the reunion in August 2025, the pair said they were taking things slow.

“I know people are expecting us to be labeled by now, and I also see comments like, ‘She better come pregnant and married to the reunion,’” Nic said. “We’ve always been believers in taking our time with things and not trying to let outside pressure dictate our relationship, and I mean, we’re going on trips together. We have future dates planned, knocking some things off the list ... Whatever she wants, I want to make sure it happens.”

As recently as June 2026, Olandria said that the two were still hanging out, but aimed to keep the details of their relationship private. She told Cosmopolitan that they go to dinner, watch movies together and have even taken a motorcycle ride with one another.

“We don’t monetize our relationship or put it on display. If you genuinely like spending quality time with somebody, it shouldn’t involve a camera every two seconds,” she told the magazine. “We enjoy each other’s presence and do what normal people do: go out, have fun, and get to know each other.”

title: Resurfaced Video Of Tom Holland’s Ballet Skills Has Left The Internet Stunned
summary: Tom Holland is set to portray legendary dancer Fred Astaire in an upcoming biopic. A resurfaced video in which he shows off his ballet skills proves why he’s perfect for the role.
story: Well, this should clear up any questions around actor Tom Holland’s dancing abilities.

Holland is set to portray legendary dancer Fred Astaire in an upcoming biopic. And because of the role, the 30-year-old has been the focus of conversation for some internet users who are unfamiliar with his strong dance background.

After one particular social media user on X recently questioned Holland’s ability to fill Astaire’s (dancing) shoes, others have been sharing an old clip of “The Odyssey” star absolutely tearing up the studio dance floor with his ballet moves.

“I think he’ll be ok!” wrote one user on X, who shared a 2017 clip of Holland, absolutely nailing some perfect turns on the floor of the Royal Ballet School in London. Unsurprisingly, the post went viral, drawing upwards of 161,000 likes.
In the clip, Holland completes a series of fouette turns with pretty impeccable control.
“The turns he’s doing here are so hard,” one social media user wrote on X. “The point is to make it look effortless but these are…so incredibly hard. I love this casting, honestly.”

The video actually comes from a seven-minute short film, produced by the London-based Flett Films, about Joel Kioko, a ballet dancer who grew up in a slum in Kuwinda, Kenya. Kioko, who was eventually able to secure a scholarship at the English National Ballet School, had the opportunity to dance with Holland while auditioning in London, according to the film’s description.
In the short film, Holland marveled at their shared appreciation for dance.

“It’s an amazing form of communication. You know, I’ve learned my dance moves in London,” Holland tells Kioko in the film. “You’ve learned your dance moves in Africa, but they’re the same dance moves.”

Holland, whose busy summer includes promoting films “The Odyssey” and the upcoming Marvel movie “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” comes from a heavy dance background. In fact, he trained in ballet, tap and acrobatics for the titular role in the West End production of “Billy Elliot the Musical.” He was just 12 years old when he debuted as Billy Elliot.
His dance skills and physicality were among the reasons why Holland was given the role of Spider-Man, several who’ve worked on Marvel projects have said.
You’ve clearly got this, Tom!

title: Iran vows to ‘punish the aggressor today’ after U.S. unleashes ‘heavy wave’ of strikes
summary: The conflict appeared to draw in new countries, as Egypt confirmed that a drone hit two natural gas vessels at one of its ports.
story: Iran vowed to “punish” the United States on Thursday after the American military said it had completed a “heavy wave of strikes” overnight, the latest retaliation for an attack by Tehran on U.S. forces in the Middle East.
The renewed fighting shattered a brief period of calm that had seen the two sides engage with a push to revive diplomatic efforts and stave off dramatic new escalation.

But President Donald Trump said the U.S. would hit Iran hard after its attack on an American base in Jordan. And the powerful Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) signaled the flare-up would not end there, warning early Thursday that “the aggressor will be punished today” following the U.S. strikes.
Jordan said it intercepted a new barrage from Iran, while Kuwait said an Iranian strike hit a building belonging to a Chinese company, killing one worker.
There were also signs that the war was again expanding and drawing in new countries, raising the stakes for the region and the global economy.
After Saudi Arabia joined the U.S. in striking Iran-backed militants in Iraq, Egypt confirmed Thursday that a drone ignited fires on two natural gas vessels at the Mediterranean port of Damietta.

Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman met with Trump and Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday to relay a message from Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman that the kingdom is not looking to escalate the war with Iran, according to a source familiar with the matter.
The separate meetings came within 24 hours of the joint U.S. and Saudi strikes against Iran-backed militants in Iraq, according to a White House official.
The discussions were first reported by Axios.

In his meetings, the defense minister conveyed that the Iranian militias had crossed a line and Saudi Arabia will not tolerate anyone attacking their civilian infrastructure or energy facilities, the source said. He also emphasized that the strikes were to demonstrate Saudi Arabia’s capacity to defend itself when needed and not an indication of support for escalation.
The Saudis believe that any escalation would involve unknown risks and likely prolong the war, which is not the path they desire for the region, the source said.

It was not immediately clear who was behind the drone strikes — on a U.S.-owned floating storage facility and a Greek-owned tanker — in Egypt but an attack there by Iran would mark a significant new expansion of the conflict to a key U.S. ally and mediator. It would also highlight the broader risk to the world’s energy supplies from the difficulty in resolving the conflict.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Thursday that Egypt is an “important friend” in a post on X.

“Egypt is an important friend and partner in the region, and its security is of utmost importance to us,” he wrote. “We must all be vigilant against Israeli plots and false-flag operations designed to undermine regional peace.”
Asked if Iran was responsible for the Egypt attack during an Oval Office event Wednesday, Trump said that he had been briefed on the incident and that “it’s a little more of the same.”
“It’s going to be straightening out,” he added, without expanding on what exactly he meant. “In the meantime, we’re going to be hitting them very hard because it’s our turn to hit them.”
Trump also vowed Wednesday to “beat the f---ing s--- out of” Iran after its Tuesday attack on American forces, according to Fox News, which cited a phone call with the president.

title: U.S. strikes Iran after Trump reportedly issues menacing new threat
summary: The fighting shattered a brief period of calm after weeks of escalation between the U.S. and Iran over the strategic Strait of Hormuz.
story: The U.S. military attacked Iran on Wednesday after President Donald Trump vowed to “beat the f---ing s--- out of” the country, according to Fox News, following new attacks on American forces in the Middle East.
“They’re going to get a beating,” Trump said, according to Fox’s chief foreign correspondent, Trey Yingst.
U.S. Central Command said a “heavy wave of strikes” had been completed at 10 p.m. ET, two hours after they began.
The strikes on dozens of targets “aimed to further diminish threats posed by Iran and its proxies to American forces, commercial shipping, and neighboring Gulf countries,” the command said on X.
The comments followed what the U.S. described as a “surprise attack,” which prompted Saudi Arabia and the U.S. to retaliate against a Tehran-backed militia in Iraq.

Iran had suspended its attacks amid a renewed push to reach a deal with the U.S., but it warned this week that it would not allow Washington to dictate the “timing of war and peace” and maintained that the Strait of Hormuz was “closed.”
The sudden return of hostilities shattered the relative calm that had descended on Iran for several days after the U.S. paused daily strikes on the Islamic Republic to make room for peace talks.

Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it launched strikes on a U.S. air base and military central command center in Jordan, state-run Nour News agency reported early Wednesday local time. Its navy also struck three oil tankers that it said were “in violation” of its blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, according to the state-run news agency IRNA.

U.S. Central Command, or CENTCOM, said on X that it had thwarted an “attempted surprise attack” on forces based in the Middle East around 5:45 p.m. Tuesday. All Iranian missiles were intercepted, it said, but troops remained “vigilant and at a high state of readiness.”

Just hours later, CENTCOM said it had launched “precision strikes” in Iraq alongside the Saudi armed forces against “Iran-aligned terrorists” that it said the IRGC had directed to attack U.S. forces and Saudi energy infrastructure.

title: K-pop group BTS won’t submit its music for Grammy Awards
summary: “I hope that music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” the group said in a statement.
story: K-pop sensation BTS said Wednesday that it will not submit its music for consideration at the 2027 Grammy Awards, citing concerns over category divisions.
The seven members — RM, Jimin, V, Suga, Jungkook, Jin and j-Hope — uploaded the same statement to their individual Instagram accounts.
“We have decided not to enter the Grammys this year,” a translation of the message read. “I hope that music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language.”

The hugely popular group from South Korea was widely expected to be nominated for some of the Recording Academy’s top accolades at the 69th Grammy Awards — including album of the year. The boyband’s most recent album, “Arirang,” has been one of the bestselling records of the year.
The album’s lead single, “Swim,” was a Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 hit in the United States.

Under the new categorizations, “Swim” might have been excluded from competing for best Asian pop music performance, one of the five new categories the Recording Academy announced last month. The new award categories were sold as an effort to boost inclusivity.

While a lot of BTS’ songs are in Korean, the lead track is mostly sung in English. A rulebook for the Grammy Awards specifies that the recordings for the new award “must feature meaningful use of one or more Asian languages.”
“An Asian language should play a significant role within the song in bilingual or multilingual structures such that the recording is identifiable with that language,” the rulebook reads.
Grammys CEO Harvey Mason Jr. said in a statement Wednesday that he was saddened by the group’s decision “but as a music creator, I understand and respect their decision.”
He said the Asian Pop category was created to celebrate “the depth, diversity and extraordinary growth of pop artistry coming out of Asia.”
“More categories mean more artists’ work is recognized. It’s never to divide, but to expand who is recognized by our 15,000 Grammy voters,” Mason said.
He noted that submitting music in a specific genre category doesn’t exclude artists from also submitting and being considered  general categories, such as Song of the Year.
Mason said the Grammys will “continue to listen to the global music community and work to honor and celebrate all the artists whose music moves the world.”

BTS, which formed in 2013 and has been compared to The Beatles, has previously performed at the Grammys and was the first K-pop act to receive a Grammy nomination. It has earned five nominations but so far hasn’t won.

BTS stands for the Korean phrase “Bangtan Sonyeondan,” which translates to “Bulletproof Boy Scouts.” The band has a huge global following and recently performed in the United States during the World Cup final’s halftime show.
On Wednesday, the group thanked its fans for their support.
“Thank you to Army and everyone who is always with us,” the band said.

title: At least 13 killed in Japan earthquake as rescuers search for survivors in a ‘race against time’
summary: Multiple people were missing a day after a magnitude-7.1 quake struck Kumamoto prefecture, partially collapsing buildings.
story: At least 13 people have been killed in southwestern Japan after a magnitude-7.1 earthquake, Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Wednesday, as rescuers searched for people trapped in collapsed buildings, including a shopping mall.

“Even now, there are people waiting to be rescued, and this is a race against time. We will marshal all available resources on the ground to save and rescue as many people as possible,” Takaichi told reporters in Tokyo.

The quake struck Tuesday afternoon in Kumamoto prefecture on Japan’s southern main island of Kyushu at a relatively shallow depth of 6 miles, prompting tsunami warnings and evacuation from coastal areas. The epicenter was about 12 miles south of the city of Kumamoto, which has a population of about 700,000.

While the tsunami warning was lifted shortly after, the quake caused extensive damage throughout the prefecture, including to historic buildings such as Kumamoto Castle, a popular tourist site that is still under repair from another deadly quake in the same area in 2016.
It also ruptured roads and left thousands of homes without power, with officials warning residents to beware of heatstroke as temperatures reach well into the 90s.

title: Major earthquake rocks southern Japan, injuring dozens
summary: The earthquake, which had an epicenter in the southwest part of the country, was measured at magnitude 6.8 and a depth of 10 kilometers, or just over 6 miles.
story: A 6.8-magnitude earthquake rocked southern Japan on Tuesday, forcing hundreds of thousands of people to evacuate and prompting the collapse of several buildings, including a shopping mall.
Japanese officials instructed roughly 300,000 people in the country’s southern Kumamoto prefecture to seek shelter at evacuation centers.
Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said Wednesday morning local time that 13 people have been found dead and many other people were injured or still missing as rescue work continued overnight.

The Japan Meteorological Agency said the earthquake, with a preliminary magnitude of 7.1 and depth of just over 6 miles, was at the highest end of the seismic intensity scale. The U.S. Geological Survey later revised its measurement to magnitude 6.8. Its epicenter was about 12 miles south of Kumamoto, central Kyushu island’s largest city, with a population of around 700,000, according to officials.

The Japanese Cabinet Office’s disaster management division said the earthquake struck around 4:27 p.m. local time (3:27 a.m. ET), with a tsunami advisory issued for the Ariake and Yatsushiro seas minutes later. The warning was later lifted, state broadcaster NHK reported.

An unknown number of people were trapped in a shopping mall, according to fire officials, who said an explosion had been heard on the building’s second floor. Twenty to 30 mall employees were unaccounted for, NHK reported.

Commercial broadcaster TBS quoted local police as saying “quite a few” people are believed to have been killed after the explosion. A second broadcaster, Fuji TV, said that multiple deaths had been confirmed at the mall.
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google
State broadcaster NHK carried footage of almost a dozen fire trucks in the facility’s parking lot. Images also showed the mall’s collapsed ceilings and facade and a debris-littered road.
Several other buildings were also damaged, video from the region showed. At least 12 houses collapsed, and at least 50 people were injured.

Aerial footage from NHK showed that a chimney at a Nippon Paper Industries plant in Yatsushiro, a city in the Kumamoto prefecture, had partially collapsed. Local police said that several people who work at the plant are unaccounted for.
“We are gathering information on whether there are any casualties, but we are concerned because we cannot reach them,” a spokesperson for the plant told NHK.

A verified video from the city showed that a rupture on the Kyushu Expressway had trapped vehicles. NHK showed aerial images of an elevated stretch of the highway where two sections had become misaligned.
Train services around the Kyushu island were suspended, rail operator JR Kyushu said.
Takaichi said in a statement that 300 service members were being dispatched to the disaster zone.

“The government will spare no effort in emergency disaster response measures, with the highest priority placed on saving lives and rescue operations led by local police and fire departments,” her office said in a statement.
“Strong tremors, earthquakes of similar intensity may continue to occur over approximately the next week,” the statement added.

title: Search for North Carolina woman Liz Waddell is still a missing person case, Grenada police say
summary: Grenadian police said their nearly week-old search for a missing North Carolina woman is still active, with hopes of finding the swimmer alive.
story: Grenadian police said Tuesday that their nearly week-old search for a missing North Carolina woman is still active, with hopes of finding the swimmer alive.
Elizabeth “Liz” Waddell, a 44-year-old Cary resident, was last seen going out for a swim at Grand Anse Beach on Wednesday, the Royal Grenada Police Force said.

“At this time, the matter continues, continues to be treated as a missing person investigation,” acting Commissioner of Police Randy Connaught told reporters Tuesday. “I repeat, at this time, the matter continues to be treated as a missing person.”
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google
Surveillance cameras captured Waddell walking on a jetty near the water at 11:36 a.m. the morning she went missing, Connaught said.
She went into the water at 11:51 a.m. and more footage captured her swimming under the jetty at 12:04 p.m., the police official said.
Witnesses have told investigators they later saw Waddell in the open water, police said.
Waddell’s traveling partner was captured on surveillance cameras on the beach at 12:46 p.m. and she reported the swimmer missing to police at 5:50 p.m., Connaught added.
“There is nothing questionable about her account of the investigations and we continue to receive cooperation from her,”  Connaught said of the traveling companion.
Even though Waddell hasn’t been seen in nearly six days, police said they still seek to rescue her.
“It is our hope that Elizabeth will be found and found alive and well,” Connaught said. “The Royal Grenada Police Force remains equally hopeful that she will be safe and that she is safe.”
Local police had been appealing to fishermen, boat operators and residents along the southern coastline to keep their eyes peeled for medium-build woman with short blond hair.
Waddell and her friend first arrived in Grenada, the island nation in the eastern Caribbean Sea that’s about 100 miles north of Venezuela, on July 11.
The missing woman’s husband has since come to the island to help in the search effort, officials said.

“Any bit of information will do at this time, and we do hope that we can locate Elizabeth very soon,” Connaught said. “Again, we empathize with the family, relatives and friends, and we are hopeful that Elizabeth will be found alive. Thank you.”

title: Oil prices slide as U.S. and Iran pause strikes to give ‘space’ for diplomacy
summary: The two sides halted fire over the weekend, following 13 nights of attacks that threatened new pain for the global economy.
story: Oil prices tumbled Monday as the United States and Iran paused their escalating strikes to make “space” for diplomacy.
The two sides halted fire over the weekend, following 13 consecutive nights of attacks that shattered their deal to end the war and threatened new pain for the global economy.
International oil benchmark Brent closed down by 8.7%, at $88.36 per barrel, while U.S. crude fell by 7.5% to $82.61 per barrel.
The moves were a sharp and rapid reversal from last week, when prices gained more than 9% and Brent rose as high as $102. Last week was oil’s third straight week of gains.

Prices fell to nearly their lowest levels of the day after President Donald Trump told reporters aboard Air Force One that the U.S. was talking with Iran “right now.” He added that he was not in a rush to make a deal and had “plenty of time” for talks.

Stocks broadly rallied earlier in the day, but those gains faded as the day progressed. By late afternoon trading, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq were flat. The Dow still had a slight gain of about 200 points.
U.S. Treasury yields, which steer consumer borrowing rates, declined only slightly and were still near the highest level since early 2025.

The renewed optimism follows mounting fears of a return to all-out war across the Middle East, as the battle for control of the crucial Strait of Hormuz expanded to the Red Sea, another key waterway for global trade.
Iran has launched several drones at ships in the strait in the past several days, according to a U.S. official, who noted that the U.S. military shot down the drones and no ships were impacted.
Iranian-backed militias also continue to target U.S. interests, U.S. forces and partners in Iraq, the official said. The U.S. has also been defending against those attacks.
Trump said Thursday that he was considering a “massive attack” to try to break Iran’s grip on the strait, but since then the U.S. and Iran have refrained from attacks for three days.
The U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, Mike Waltz, told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” on Sunday that the decision to halt strikes came in response to ongoing talks between the two sides.

“What the president is doing right now, as we’ve seen all along, is giving some talks some space,” he said, adding that talks were “ongoing” but that there was “internal fighting” on the Iranian side.
Waltz dismissed reporting that U.S. weapons stockpiles are depleted.
Still, Tehran offered limited hope for any ramped-up peace efforts.

“Mediators may convey messages from the American side to us concerning regional developments, but at the present time we have no negotiations with the American side,” Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Monday at a news conference.
He said Tehran would “never allow America to determine the timing of war and peace” and would “continue to defend ourselves for as long as our interests and considerations require.”
Baghaei maintained that the Strait of Hormuz was “closed.”

Oil prices had soared above $100 per barrel last week for the first time in two months as the conflict spiraled, with Hormuz effectively blocked and new disruption from attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in the Red Sea.
Shipping traffic through Hormuz was limited over the weekend, with more activity visible through the Bab el Mandeb choke point.

Along the Strait of Hormuz, just 29 verified transits were recorded from Friday to Sunday, according to an NBC News analysis of MarineTraffic data. Activity fell from 12 crossings Friday to six Saturday, before increasing to 11 Sunday.
Traffic along Bab el Mandeb remained higher, with 100 verified crossings over the same period. Daily activity was broadly stable, with 35 crossings Friday, 31 Saturday and 34 Sunday.
Prior to the war, some 20% of the world’s oil had passed through the Strait of Hormuz, with its repeated closure sending energy prices soaring and global markets tumbling throughout the conflict.
“The market seems to be forever seeking good news from an arena that really is not providing any,” PVM analyst John Evans said.

“A stay of military strikes might seem an improvement, but it does not come with any guarantees that oil will soon flow from the area. ... Prices will only continue lower if high prices once again dent demand, not questionable mini-ceasefires,” Evans said.

On Monday, the semiofficial Iranian Tasnim news agency reported that six vessels had attempted to pass through Hormuz “by switching off their navigation and position systems.” It said one of them “suffered an incident” while the others were returned to the Persian Gulf “under Iran’s decisive management.”

Jordan, a key U.S. ally, said it downed two drones early Monday, though it was not clear who launched them. Saudi Arabia said it intercepted and destroyed drones fired by Iran-backed militants in Iraq.
Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu made his way to Washington on Monday, with plans to discuss Iran in a meeting with Trump set for Tuesday.
“Our objective is to safeguard our security while also expanding the circle of peace around us,” Netanyahu said in comments prior to his departure.

He also noted that he was traveling to the U.S. to pay his final respects at the funeral of the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, R-S.C., whom Netanyahu described as “one of the greatest friends Israel has ever had.”
Beyond the Middle East, attacks between Russia and Ukraine have also increasingly focused on shipping, adding another complication for markets.

The Iranian Foreign Ministry accused Ukraine over the weekend of attacking an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea, saying one sailor was killed and another injured. The ministry summoned Ukraine’s chargé d’affaires in Tehran in protest.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv had ‌noted Russia ⁠was passing on to Iran its satellite observations in the Middle East to enable Tehran to direct strikes in the region.

title: Berlin police kill suspect in Pride festival attack after manhunt
summary: Authorities say the 21-year-old was fatally shot after charging at officers with a knife, a day after an attack left one dead and 29 injured.
story: Berlin police shot and killed the suspect in this weekend’s deadly attack during the city’s Pride festival after he allegedly charged at officers with a knife while they tried to arrest him Sunday, authorities said.

The 21-year-old suspect was found at 6 p.m. local time at an allotment garden complex in the Spandau district, Berlin police said. Authorities said he rushed at members of the city’s special police unit, or SEK, with a weapon, prompting officers to open fire. Despite firefighters’ resuscitation efforts, he died at the scene.
Authorities have accused the suspect of driving a vehicle into a crowd and attacking people with a bladed weapon near Brandenburg Gate on Saturday night, killing a woman and injuring 29 others.
Three of the injured people have life-threatening injuries, Berlin’s fire department spokesman Dominik Pretz said Sunday morning, adding that eight are seriously injured.

Police identified the suspect as 21-year-old Abdul B., whom officials describe as a “radicalized” member of “Islamist circles” in Berlin. The country’s Interior Ministry later released the suspect’s last name, Ballout.
“Everything we are seeing here indicates that we have experienced an Islamist attack,” German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said at a news conference Sunday.

He identified the suspect as a German citizen of Lebanese background known to police after committing crimes in the past. Ballout had previously been sentenced to one year and 10 months in prison in Berlin, he said, which was commuted to parole.

He was sentenced for preparing a serious act of violence endangering the state and violating an enforceable prohibition under the Associations Act, the Office of the Berlin Public Prosecutor General said in a statement. The sentence was handed down in May.

The office said the verdict was based on information that he had attempted to travel to Syria last year to join the Islamic State group but was arrested in Lebanon, where he was in contact with several people he believed were members of the group and was sentenced to three months in prison, in part for incitement to religious and sectarian conflict. After that, the office said, he returned to Germany, was arrested at Berlin Brandenburg Airport and was held in pretrial detention until the verdict.

The office said the court found that he had “published prohibited IS propaganda on his Instagram account on June 16 and 24, 2024.” In determining the sentence, the court considered the three months he was held in Lebanon and the six months he spent in pretrial detention in Germany, the office said.

It also “took into account that Abdul B. had largely confessed during the trial, distanced himself from ISIS, and that there had been no concrete threat to protected legal interests,” the office said.

Before that, he had been convicted of assaulting someone at a Berlin high school in 2019, as well as robbing someone of a pair of headphones nearly a year later. He was also convicted in 2022 of assault and robbery by extortion, the office said.
Earlier this month, Berlin prosecutors searched his home for firearms but found only a toy gun, and the case was dismissed.
Hundreds of thousands of people had gathered in Berlin for one of Europe’s largest LGBTQ+ celebrations. The parade had passed through the park earlier Saturday.

The attack was outside the secure festival area, Dobrindt said, adding that many of those attacked were going to or from the festival site. A vehicle used in the attack was removed from the scene Sunday.
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has condemned the incident in Berlin as “a heinous act.”
“They wanted us to treat each other with kindness and tolerance. This is an attack on our society,” he wrote on X, adding that the attack will be investigated with the “utmost severity.”
Saturday “should have been a day of joy, visibility and freedom,” Alfonso Pantisano, the Berlin state government’s queer liaison officer, wrote on social media.
European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen expressed her sympathy to the victims Sunday, saying the Pride event stands for “freedom, dignity, and equality.”
“Every person should be able to live, love, and stand up for their rights without fear,” she wrote on social media.

title: U.S. forgoes strikes on Iran, but conflict in the Red Sea escalates
summary: U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” that the pause in strikes was due to ongoing talks between the two countries.
story: The Iran war ​broadened over the weekend despite a pause in U.S. strikes, as Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis attacked Saudi oil installations along the Red Sea coast and Iran ‌accused Ukraine of targeting one of its vessels in the Caspian Sea.
The U.S. military said Saturday that its naval blockade against Iran “remains in full effect” but did not explain why it halted a streak of 13 nights of escalating strikes.
There were also no weekend reports of attacks by Iran on neighbors, similar to its daily rejoinders to the U.S. attacks.
U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” that a pause in strikes was due to ongoing talks between the two countries.
“What the president is doing right now, as we’ve seen all along, is giving some talks some space,” he said. “Talks are ongoing.”
Waltz added that while talks were ongoing at the highest levels of the Iranian and U.S. governments, there was “internal fighting” on the Iranian side.
“Some are seeking the guidance of the supreme leader,” he said. “Others want to move into a different direction, and that makes it hugely challenging.”
Iran ​will halt its own attacks as long as the United ⁠States maintains its pause on strikes, but Tehran remains skeptical of U.S. ⁠intentions, a ​senior Iranian source told Reuters on Sunday.

“Iran’s ⁠position remains ‘attack for attack’: ​if ⁠the attacks stop, ‌Iran will also halt its operations. That message ‌has already been conveyed ‌to the United States,” the source told Reuters, ⁠a day after Washington halted attacks following 13 successive nights of airstrikes.
“There is more skepticism than optimism about ‌the halt in attacks. ​The prevailing view ‌is that ⁠the pause is ⁠tactical rather than genuine,” the ‌source added.
Trump has decided, for now, to back away from plans to ramp up attacks on Iran, ⁠The New York Times reported Saturday, citing two people briefed on the discussion.

The president and his advisers, the newspaper said, have concerns about expanding the conflict, depleting ​defense stockpiles, alienating Middle East Gulf allies and affecting energy supplies and the global economy.

Vice President JD Vance and Gen. Dan Caine, the chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, ​both raised concerns about the U.S. munitions stockpile with Trump during a White House meeting on Friday, a U.S. official told CNN.
Operations are “on a hold,” a Department of Defense source told the broadcaster on Saturday.

Despite the Gulf lull, Saturday’s fighting between Iran’s Houthi allies and Saudi Arabia showed that the war, which has already disrupted energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, could affect a second major ​shipping route and reignite Yemen’s civil war.
Separately, Iran’s Foreign Ministry accused Ukraine of attacking an Iranian commercial vessel in the Caspian Sea, saying one sailor was killed and another injured.
The ​ministry summoned Ukraine’s chargé d’affaires in Tehran to protest over an attack it described as “hostile and criminal,” state news agency IRNA said.

The Iranian denunciation coincided with comments by Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that Kyiv had ‌noted Russia ⁠was passing on to Iran its satellite observations in the Middle East to enable it to direct strikes in the region.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the group struck sites belonging to Saudi state oil company Aramco in the cities of Jizan and Yanbu on Saturday.

A large column of smoke rose from the direction of the Aramco refinery in Jizan, near the Yemeni border, video on social media verified by Reuters showed. The refinery can process up to 400,000 barrels of crude oil ​daily.
Two Asia-based trading sources said they had been ​informed of potential damage to fuel ⁠and oil storage sites at Jizan. Aramco did not respond to requests for comment.

In Yanbu, two missiles aimed at oil installations were intercepted. Yanbu, Saudi Arabia’s main Red Sea oil port, has become a key route for Saudi oil skirting the Strait of Hormuz, ​which Iran has blockaded.

In Yemen, officials said the air force of the Saudi-backed, internationally recognized government, which has ​opposed the Houthis for ⁠more than a decade, struck Houthi sites in the Marib and al-Jawf provinces.
The officials said both sides in Yemen’s civil war were mobilizing forces along the front.
Saudi Arabia has led an Arab coalition battling the Houthis since the Iran-aligned fighters captured Yemen’s capital, Sanaa.
The civil war, in which famine and fighting killed hundreds of thousands, has been paused by a ceasefire since ⁠2022.
But that ​truce broke down this month, with the Houthis effectively joining the wider war their Iranian allies have ​waged since being attacked by the United States and Israel five months ago.
The Houthis have declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia over the past week, and Houthi leader Abdul Malik al-Houthi said all Saudi oil ​facilities could be targets.

title: ‘Cockroaches won’: India’s youth protest leaders declare victory as minister resigns
summary: India’s viral Cockroach Janta Party called off its nationwide protests Saturday after the country’s education minister resigned and the government agreed to a number of the activist movement’s demands.
